analysis.name: Alaron Lewis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lewis is very nice and she is available to help outside of class when needed. However, her lectures do not go by the book and go outside the contents and expects you to know information she hasnt clearly taught. She made the midterm exam harder than the practice exam and expected us to finish in the time frame and even said sorry to us.

Dr. Lewis is one of the only professors in my experience that explains topics in a way that is easy to understand. She provides practice exams, a LOT of worksheets (they are super helpful, though), she records her lectures, and even hosts online web conferences the night before an exam. By far one of the best BIO professors. I highly recommend!

Really fun and chill professor. I felt that students were pretty comfortable talking to her and asking questions or making jokes. Exams are not that hard and there's homework, participation, and lab to prop up your grade. Only cons are that lab is a lot of work and missing a class hurts because most info is in lecture and slides lack information.

Dr Lewis is a really dedicated professor to her students and class! She enjoys what she teaches and it clearly shows. Asking questions outside the class was really helpful to my learning and she wants the success for all her students. Its definitely hard to learn just off her slides, so try and attend class!

GREAT FOR MCAT REVIEW! very writing heavy. Every week you will have a writing assignment paired with homework questions; there is a final paper, mid term, and final exam. Rarely gives 100% in writing. Expect constant feedback and criticism! She can be blunt in person but passionate. Verbal explainer. Video lectures are what you expect.

analysis.name: Baaska Anderson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Anderson's lecture approach was very accessible. I was a bit wary of stats, but very happy that I took it with her. I felt comfortable asking questions and she checked in frequently with students to make sure they were following the material. I really enjoyed her style.

The class is very self paced. She has pre filmed lectures that aren't amazing but will pretty much walk you through how to do the assignments. 1 quiz and 1 assignment every 2 weeks and no attendance requirements. Overall ok class, I'd take her again but just bc it was an easy class. She also asks you to buy the textbook but i didn't open it once...

As long as you read the textbook, watch her online lectures, and do the assignments and quizzes, you'll pass this class easily. There's also not much work to do; there are only 5 modules with plenty of time to finish them (2 weeks each). I went to class in person once this whole quarter.

if you need a statistics credit, definitely take her class. you don't have to go to class if you can do the work on time (which is very manageable - like 1 assignment per 2 weeks). the final was take home and you had like a week to do it. also, all material is available from day 1 so you can do it completely at your own pace!

She's a little strange, I requested some help online and when we joined Zoom, she didn't have her camera on, so I found that a bit strange. She's nice, but also uses outdated videos as lectures, so u have to find the new layouts. Attendance is not mandatory which is amazing.

analysis.name: Arieh Arkady Retik
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Arieh (Arkady) Retik is a GREAT professor. He is by far the best CSS professor at UW Bothell. He cares about your grades and knowledge. Be ready to read a lot. Most of the assignments are group assignments so make sure to be ready to be in a group of 3 other hard workers. This is really important. He grades very fairly and is nice to students.

Professor Retik is a chill guy. Lectures are clear and engaging. The class is team-based - make sure you create or join a good team. There are quite a few short presentations (mostly group-based) in the quarter and there's an emphasis on improving your presentation skills. Some quizzes are tricky but are curved and allow cheat sheets and critique.

There isn't any hard-coding that you need to do for this class, as the project just focuses on the development (1 deliverable weekly) of a plan for a theoretical project that you don't have to do. Besides the project, the homework and tests are pretty easy. Just read the parts of the textbooks specified by the lectures, and this class is an easy A.

One of the worst professors I've had. Very vague grading criteria so you need to be good at reading his mind. Expects you to take a quiz that is meant to be 45 minutes in like 20 minutes. Cannot explain a concept in a proper manner. Jumps from topic to topic. You just hear him talking on and on but don't understand the point he's trying to make.

Not the best lecturer, but overall he's really nice and easy to work with. The group project/assignment guidelines can be hard to understand, but don't hesitate to talk to him and ask for clarification. If you're having any issues with the class, just talk to him - he's very responsive and will work with you. Pretty funny too.

analysis.name: Jyoti Agrawal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Jyoti Agrawal was a very good professor. She made efforts to make sure students understood the topics we learned in class and encouraged class participation. Homework and exams were done on Pearson. You were allowed a cheat sheet during exams. Overall, great professor who knows what she is talking about. 100% reccomend

She isn't a bad teacher but sometimes her phrasing and teaching style can be confusing, which made it a little difficult to understand since the class uses Excel and math I hadn't seen before. Pay attention when she goes over it, go to class, read the text book, ask questions, DO THE EXTRA CREDIT! You got this :)

ppl aren't lying when they say that asking questions in class feels like a humiliation ritual. felt very condescending and honestly made me hate operations. i definitely wish i had taken the course with the other operations prof and hope you do too.

I dont like her. She is very harsh to students and does not hesitate to tell you,  you are wrong. Asking questions feels like setting yourself up to be humiliated. Slides dont match the book which won't match the test. Hard class content in general.

2 group projects (30%), 2 exams (35%, no make-ups), HW 25% w/ 12% late penalty and can be accepted up to 2 days before exam, in-class quizzes are 10% (2-3 quizzes), lecture slides on Canvas, use of Microsoft Excel, instructor encourages engagement and questions

analysis.name: Christian Anderson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He didn't grade some assignments for a while so I didn't get feedback on them until after I turned the next assignment in, which would then effect my grade on the next assignment due to not knowing how I did. He grades pretty harsh so you have to be really specific with including everything he wants, even if it seems like you already did.

Professor Anderson is a great professor! He is VERY kind and understanding. He wants to see his students succeed and will support you. His assignments were very fun to do, I oddly looked forward to doing them. Great teacher and class set up. I def recommend

I've never had a professor who's been able to make an asynchronous online course as engaging as Professor Anderson. He is passionate about what he teaches and very understanding. It's clear he cares about his students and he wants them all to succeed!

The class is great overall, but Professor Anderson's grading does not align with the expectations of a 100-level course. Additionally, grading turnaround times are long, which negatively impacts performance on future assignments.

This professor gives more than enough time and heads-ups for their big final homework assignment-which is nice. One of the easiest classes I had this quarter, which made working 2 jobs and traveling mid-quarter for competitions really smooth. The professor is super enthusiastic about maps, and his lectures give "fun with flags" vibes.

analysis.name: Alison Lo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lo was really great! She definitely cares for her students and wants everyone to succeed. She is very blunt when it comes to your work but it helps you learn. You were allowed to resubmit any assignment if you up until the end of the quarter if you wanted to receive a better grade. tests are multiple choice based on textbook.

I don't really take the time to rate professors, but Lo is by far the absolute best professor I have ever had. Even after taking her class and parting ways, she's still advocating for me. Put in the effort into her class, show her you're motivated, and you'll have someone in your corner for years to come.

Pretty easy class. Only had to show up a few times for group presentations, but otherwise everything is online and very easy. the midterm and final you can use a sheet of notes. i will say she is not a great lecturer. really rambles on and isn't very clear. but, the course overall was organized and clear. Pearson is used for all assignments.
Professor Lo is one of the first professors who seemed to care for her students. Her lectures are a little bit hard to grasp but her homework assignments really taught me a lot.

THICK accent. She doesn't really talk to the class during her lectures (which don't even matter because there aren't tests or quizzes, or anything pertaining to them). Class is basically group work and two individual case studies. Final is extra credit. By far the easiest teacher  class ever.

analysis.name: Andrew Abian
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor uses OneNote which lets you study ahead and makes notes the professor writes during teaching a lot more accessible for studying. The professor sometimes makes mistakes with scheduling due dates online but often changes them and you don't get marked down for missing them. There's group cold calling as well. Exams based on group work.

The structure of the class is.. unconventional, to say the least. You're expected to watch lecture videos at home, complete a quiz on the lesson before class, and then class is just worksheets. Then you also have homework based on the lesson, so overall, it's just a lot of work. Attendance is not mandatory; you'd probably learn more alone, anyway.

I took STMATH 124. The professor is a nice person. However, the professor never checks his emails or canvas messages. The professor also sometimes assigns assignments late at night and makes it due early the next day. The professor does not really teach well and is disorganized. I would only recommend this professor if you have no options left.

Y'all are hating, yes he is disorganized but you never have to deal with the consequences of it. He will make mistakes but it will never effect your grade just point them out and he will fix it. He is passionate about his teaching and he is very helpful if you have question. I could not recommend him enough.

-Attendance isn't required. 
-Required to watch a video and take notes on worksheets before class.
-Classes include group work. 
-Homework assignments are on MyMathLab.
-Can be disorganized and doesn't always let us know when due dates and lock dates are adjusted.
-Class is easy to pass if you do all of the work.
-Drops the lowest test score.

analysis.name: Anne Richards
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Easiest grader ever, no final (just weekly 8-question quizzes). Provides free textbook, very textbook reading heavy homework but overall not too bad. Lectures are a bit repetitive to what we read in the textbook but interactive activities every lecture. Super understanding, allows late work. So so sweet. :)

She was a very kind professor and gives a clear guideline of what to expect for the quarter. There is a lot of reading and weekly quizzes but it's not a lot and pretty easy since it was online quizzes and you can use your notes. The lectures every week though felt boring as it feels like she repeats what we read in our textbook (Homework Notes).

This is the second class I've taken with Professor Richards and she is lovely. Super easy grader and assignment load. We had chapter readings that go along with the weekly homework assigment and weekly quizzes. Attendance is needed if you want full credit for the in-class assignments. She emails back quickly and is very sweet! I highly recommned!

Her class was fun and super easy! However, I do think she could spice up her lectures to make them entertaining, but it was prob the easiest class I've taken, so I can't complain. Otherwise, all the information in the class is very eye-opening. Def take her classes!

analysis.name: Alka Kurian
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: LOVED this course, and the professor is helpful, understanding, funny, flexible and keeps the class interesting. I highly recommend to take this class. However, you absolutely need to attend class and do the participation exercises to get the benefit of it

Her class is discussion based but She wants to discuss alot of issues without offending people which isnt really possible. She makes things super complicated when they are not complicated.I had a major career thing clashing w final exam and she was super un-supportive about it and kept like delaying her response to me  which i found annoying.

She is a nice person. EZ course works. I told her I was sick at presentation day. She just give me full points with it. But she is kinda tough to grade. I submit all assignments and going class everyday only got 2.5 gpa. two exams were kinda hard to international students.

I took BISGWS 301, I really enjoyed Professor Kurian's lectures, there's a lot of in class discussions (not mandatory to speak unless its group discussions). There's weekly (long) readings that you annotate once each page, and a 10-15 min group presentation. It's a lot of heavy thinking but doable.

-Annotations assignments (movies and readings, on things that stood out + agree/disagree with, can be submitted up to 2 weeks post-deadline)
-2 exams (written)
-Extra credit (time stamps for theme + short answer for justification)
-Group presentation
-Class participation (do assignments in-class and online)

analysis.name: Naomi Bragin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Has to be the worst professor when it comes to grading, if you don't write to appease what she wants out of you, you get marked points for it. Every assignment she's nitpicky about taking decimal points off of your grade if she finds something she doesn't like. For an online class there is live event performance you must go to, which is insane.

For a 2 hr dance class, a majority of it was spent sitting down in a circle and listening to her yap about finding your mind. Not a nice teacher, she comes off passive-aggressive and doesn't take feedback very well. Her grading is very off, and doesnt let you see the scores you get. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if you don't want your time wasted.

She is nice, but you can tell she is very inexperienced at teaching. She will almost always just mark you down randomly and provide no comments. For our final project, every group got the exact same low grade and she gave no feedback to anyone. And the class is graded very hard, so losing even one point will drop your GPA significantly.

For an intro class, expect a huge mass amounts of homework for one week. What you won't expect is the late grading, hard scoring, and immature behavior. I understand dance is her passion, but she sucks the fun and enjoyment of the art in dance. Don't bother asking how you can succeed in this class, she will NOT be helpful.

pretty easy A but I don't recommend it for anyone that's not comfortable with getting out of their comfort zone. She'll put you on the spot to try to fix what you're doing wrong, & no matter what how or why it's always embarrassing. Her assignments are mostly discussions and not different at all. It gets frustratingly boring. not really worth it.

analysis.name: Billy Phillips
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
95%=4.0, His Lectures are fun & helpful. 
No feedback on assignments unless you ask.
He has criteria, Be sure to check them Or YOU WILL LOSE POINTS for the SLIGHTEST mistakes. 
He deducts participation points for being 1min late. Absent = 0, even excused.
Extra credit, but not enough to cover the points you lose throughout the course.
2 hw per week

Using AI is allowed as long as it is declared, and you will pass the class with ease. Mandatory attendance but beside that, everything else is chill is easy. He did not teach a lot, but it's fun class. Also, the class is a required for BBUS students so just pick an easy instructor.

Amazing professor! His level of intensity, passion, and care are second to none. The class consists of small assignments and one case study (worth most of your grade). You will spend half of the quarter working in this paper, but professor Phillips offers feedback and support to complete it. One of the best classes I've ever taken.

Awesome professor, provides honest feedback and clearly tells you what is important writing wise. He makes it known that he is there to help students. Normally I wouldn't go out of my way to waste my time posting one of these ratings but he was such a good prof that it feels deserved.

Most inspirational and best professor IU have had. Glad I started my first quarter and first UWB class ever with Billy. I hope I can take you again Professor Phillips and I hope you continue to inspire other students.

analysis.name: Alexandre Barchechat
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 114 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Awful teacher, and I do not say that about teachers almost ever. He gives packets every day with a few examples and rushed through them on the white board. he actually laughs when something is hard for us and is VERY condescending, making sarcastic and rude comments. He doesn't input any grades because "we are math students and we should do it". NO

His way teaching does not really fit my study style. He just writes everything on the board and let you take notes. I do not think he gives students enough time to think about the examples. Also, he makes hard quizzes and tests. And those quizzes can decide whether you fall or not. However, it is almost impossible to get really high grade unless you are the top 3 students. The average grade is about 65 percent for my class.

I'm confused as to why they have a 4.0 rating. Attendance mandatory cause he checks if you took notes. No lecture in class- prerecorded videos. Doesn't finish examples in videos. Doesn't believe in giving students answers so you never know if you're right. Never directly answers your question. Class just means working on problems without answers.

All his lectures are videos from 3 years ago he expects you to watch and basically master before class. Doesn't actually teach in class and throws really though problems with no solutions. Too many random assignments to keep track of. You can pick your grading contract and exams are open note but extremely difficult, all exam averages were in 60%s

Although this teacher is caring, his teaching style sucks, is a VERY tough grader, and hw does not reflect the tests at all. He hastily gives 1 or 2 examples of a concept on the board and gives a a bunch of exercises. He expects us to just understand. No one feels like calling him over for help at every single step. I learned more from self study.

analysis.name: Tim Billo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I have taken like four different classes with Tim and I think he's great. He cares a lot and as a result I have become quite passionate about a lot of enviro topics we cover. His classes are interesting and well-rounded, and he's open to feedback about assignments/class topics. There are weekly assignments and some long readings but he's worth it!

Take ENVIR 315 if you want to be bored.Tim takes us outside to play "kids" games a lot of classes.Either that or you will be listening to a discussion that everyone has to do each quarter. He assigns so much reading and more than 1000 words on each assignment. There are no tests but the amount of work makes up for that. He is also passive agressive

Get ready to read and get ready to write and walk!!! You will have multiple 1000+ word assignments per week and easily 80 pages of reading. On top of that the professor has a propensity for taking class outdoors in the middle of natural areas. I feel like I should be getting writing credit and PE credit but I'm not and you wont either. Dont take!!!

I loved this class! Tim is great. Ask to hear his songs it's super fun! I definitely learned a lot and loved the readings he assigned, there is definitely a lot of them though. Grading is a bit confusing sometimes but as long as you put full effort into everything you'll be totally good. Definitely take this class if you get a chance!

Tim is a top notch guy. I could tell he really cared about us students and the subject matter he was teaching. I gave him a 4/5 because sometimes the lectures were so dry because you just talk about the paper you read for homework. Besides that we love Tim.

analysis.name: Neil Bacon
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Had him for BPHYS 121 as my lab teacher. This dude is genuinely an AI, and will make you lose points on unclear grading criteria

It's frustrating because prof. Bacon is nice but is a tough grader (e.g. 2.9/3.0 and 0.9/1.0). The class at UWB is not difficult, but he does *not* give clear or constructive feedback on the assignments and in class. He shows you a rubric but does not explain how he applies it, making it hard for students to understand his grading criteria.

Overall he's chill and checks in with groups but doesn't give good feedback. He grades hard on lab notes so grading criteria isn't that clear. It's not a hard class though cause he doesn't focus on physics aspect more about the reflection and what you learned from it. If you have a good group then you'll be ok but no one knew what they were doing
He might know his things in physics, but he ain't good at teaching it nor explaining it
very nice person, but extremely harsh grader. dropped course due to incredulous grading. avoid at all costs, at least for lab.

analysis.name: Becca Price
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Work is difficult, especially considering it's a required course for a major that has nothing to do with the subject. Grading is extremely picky, grading guidelines un-clear, and grading scheme for the course is complicated and makes the course more difficult. Don't pick this course with this prof!!!!

One of the worst grading scales I've ever seen in my entire academic career. Unless you are deeply interested in paleontology, a lot of the material is a nightmare to go through. Micromanages a ton of the work done and will nitpick the smallest details. Nice person, though.

She makes us read assignments with over 70+ pages, and expects us to annotate all of it from start to finish. And the annotations have to actually be to her standard, so short sentences will not do. Not to mention, we have multiple of these assignments all in one week. I also did not enjoy that she talked to us like we were little kids.
Not a bad class, had its moments but I learned a lot.

She was overbearing and treated me like a child. She was over the top on sensitivity, like we do not live in the real world. I did not learn one thing within the first two weeks, not to mention any assignment we did did not correlate with anything in class.

analysis.name: Abdlmagid Basere
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The midterm and final are a large chunk of your grade and because they're practical exams they can be tricky if you don't know the equipment well. Practice the DC labs for the midterm and Practice the AC labs for the final. The transient labs were only tested in quizzes. He is not available for help most weekdays but he's a good professor.

Basere might have heard some of the feedback as he explains lab equipment well and helps when you ask for it. Worst part is that the handouts are sometimes EXTREMELY poorly written which makes it hard to do the lab. Other than that Basere is nice.

Professor Basere is a great professor! He has been teaching B EE 200 for a while now and truly wants you to succeed in the class. If you ask him a question about anything from the lab manual to the equipment he will do his best to explain it to you. Don't blame him for the lab manuals as another professor made them and just has to follow them.

For this introduction lab, you are thrown in without any knowledge on how to use a breadboard; you have to self-learn and go to the open lab on your own time. Half of the labs take more than 3 hours, which is the most time I've ever spent on a lab; however, the grading is not terrible. There is a midterm and a final. He graded nicely on the final.

This was for the 200 lab. Basere is very nice and caring but that isn't enough to make up for the unclear responses and answers to questions. He has a roundabout way of answering questions which leaves you even more confused and lost then before, the only reason I passed was because Kevin who could actually explain the why's and how's.

analysis.name: Lauren Berliner
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: super nice lady, didn't learn that much but my class was really big and i think she did her best. she's very likable and sweet and seems really knowledgeable in 1:1 conversations but the class itself wasn't that great (we watched a lot of movies/shows in class). very easy and i would take another higher level class w/ her again!

This class was great. It was super easy, you learned a lot, but it didn't require too much effort and no frustration. The workload was very appropriate and never felt unnecessary. Wasn't my favorite professor bc I didn't get a chance to connect too much, but it was a huge class, so makes sense. She was nice and understanding.

Introduction to Analyzing Media was a great course. Learnt about the technical aspects of media analysis and the external factors that influenced the production of the media works. There are two handwritten pages due every week but the topic you write about addressing the prompt is quite flexible. There are in-class discussions for participation.
Professor Berliner is super nice and encorages class discussion. Sometimes her lectures are a bit shallow and short but the class is fun.

Very nice person, could be a better teacher. Assignments are interesting but the flipped classroom format - and focus on video lectures - is not my favorite. I would've preferred more in-person lecturing rather than just doing activities and being reminded of due dates. Kinda left us hanging for the final.

analysis.name: Brandon Finley

he CANT teach, so you have to self-teach yourself CHEM!! 70% of your grade is exams. i swear he doesn't want us to learn chemistry.
i already knew a lot of chemistry, and every lecture he manages to teach in twisted ways that kind of are false. GOOD LUCK, plz be carful not to trust everything he states. 
He is also rude so don't be sensitive ig.

Oh man, just absolutely terrible. Worst professor in my entire 4-year degree. He acts like god and gatekeeper to medical school and constantly tells people to give up on being physicians if they can't ace his class? Like wtf. He treats class like a comedy skit, he has no interest in actually teaching--I'm 100% no joking. Lecture is a waste.

Very entertaining lecturer and made this class easier to tolerate. However, this is a challenging class you will have to dedicate lots of time to. Strict criteria to pass the class. If you're easily offended don't take his class; he's very blunt. However, he does care about his students and clearly loves his job. He wants to help you pass.

analysis.name: Carol Shaw
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very caring professor who cares for the success of her students. The beginning weeks are difficult with back-to-back drafts. But once those are completed, the class is a cake walk. Feedback was clear, and exams are fairly easy with a kahoot style + written portion. Overall, if you can keep up at the start, you'll be good.

Bad! She didn't allow late assignments, yet she would spend almost the entire lecture going over the previous assignment. Not to mention she would assign a LOT of work, worth a lot of points. She was a harsh grader and if you had time to ask her questions in class, she would deflect the question and then walk away while you tried to understand!

Know before taking: Attendance is mandatory, people write their names to show you were there. The course is messy, in class she would not fully help with questions, would walk away quickly. Lectures are boring and you can't really grasp what she is talking about it goes from one thing to another thing. Good thing: She did give me a good grade.

Amazing! Was very clear of feedback in instructor drafts and was a very nice professor overall! She explicitly tells you in detail why you got the grade that you got and was also very clear in lecture. One of the best 301 professors!

One of the best professors I've ever had. Very engaging with the class, and the assignments are actually useful; I learned so much and will use the skills I gained in future applications. Super caring, available outside of class, and lots of extra credit opportunities. Assignments also have very clear grading criteria, which I appreciated.

analysis.name: Ceri Nishihara
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I thought this class was Marketing Not a muscle memory class.

Undisputed GOAT professor. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it is essential for success in the class, as there are a lot of group discussions and your participation can impact your grade. There's a course pack you need to purchase and a simulation, but it isn't very expensive, and you can share it with classmates.

This is my second class with Professor Ceri, going on third. Her classes aren't structured very well and she grades harshly, but she has a lot of industry knowledge and you will learn a lot from her. Assignments apply course topics thoughtfully and quizzes are take-home and short answer.

Ceri is one of the most solid professors at UWB. She really cares about people, is very interesting, and does well with lectures. I respect her so much and wish I could take more of her classes. There is a lot to read, but it is not dry content. Get ready to LEARN a bunch of useful things. Thank you, professor! You really made my marketing journey!

Super cool professor. There is a lot of reading but as long as your do the readings and assignments on time the class is pretty easy. Engage in the discussions and argue your points and you'll be good to go.

analysis.name: Codrin Nedita
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Codrin is the best professor that I've ever had at UWB. He's extremely kind, and genuinely cares about your learning. He does anything he can to make sure everyone is with him and understands the material. Textbook is not necessary because he does such a good job at explaining material in lectures. The instructor brings lots of industry experience so we get valuable stories and insights. Projects/tests focus on the main objectives, with transparent expectations throughout. Promotes team work. Highly recommend.

Straightforward and fair. Provides excellent insights on the current industry based on extensive background (and continued work?) in the professional environment. Interact, ask questions, communicate with your group project team, do your readings and you will do well in the class.

He is a very knowledgeable professor. His expertise and industry experience can be really shown in how he teaches the course. He emphasizes on the customer and business impacts of each topic, which are very important concerns when being in the industry.

Professor Eric is an excellent professor. The course has a LOT of reading, but in his classes, he focuses only on the things that matter in real life. He also shares many of his experiences working at Microsoft, which is cool. Be ready to read. FR.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Ostrowski
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: If you are not a good test taker, do not take her class. 95% of your grade is based on 4 exams, one of which is dropped. Lectures and exams have confusing questions that she refuses to elaborate on. Dr Ostrowski is very intelligent, but did not manage to make the material understandable to students. I taught most of the material to myself.

(Genetics, not bio) Terrible professor, lectures are terrible, and study guides dont match tests. evrbody failed the test, and she insulted us instead of taking responsibility for her horrid teaching. doesn't listen at all, exam avg are 50. You have to dedicate so much time to learn bc she doesnt teach at all. Im out of words, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS

Prof.Ostrowski gives clear expectations at the beginning of the class. She also taught us how to use the equipment in the lab in the beginning of the quarter. She gave room for discussion and had us practice presenting to ensure we do great at the symposium. Most of the work was prepared by us students to give us independence for our research.

I don't think this is 100% the professor's fault but the way bio 200 lab is structured is very bad. No procedures you have to make your own. Read some random links and hope you have the right procedure. You can change it later. But the professor was kinda passive aggressive and not too approachable. Final group presentation at the end with prof.
for your gpa's sake, dont. many students are considering dropping her class. tough grader, lecture heavy. wait for another professor to teach this course.

analysis.name: Arian Eyal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Seems like a decent person, but his teaching mechanics are definitely off. For classes, he just goes over problems that you already solved, nothing that is insightful or helpful. Then, when quiz grades don't turn out good. he rubs the blame on the students. Pretty much, I can read the textbook for 10 mins and learn his 2 hours worth of lecture.
He was super rude and disrespectful. Over 2/3s of the class failed the midterm. Then he proceeded to tell us well never succeed in college because we have no work ethic.

He is a math teacher, so he teaches the mathematical concepts really well and focuses on them more. His tests were really hard, far harder than his in class examples, but he cares. This was clearly his first time teaching this course so his class was unorganized and he relied too much on his graders and didn't always explain programming as well.

Prof Arian, is a very nice guy you can tell he's passionate about CS. Class consists of 4 labs, 5 weekly quizzes and inClass labs. His directions for labs are not very clear and doesn't clearly list the expected output. His lectures are very math heavy on topics like proofs, propositions, quantifiers, recurrence relations etc. Be sure you know C++

Have one assignment/quiz a week. Do not turn it in late. He does not care what you have going on in your life, you better get it in on time. Even with DRS accommodations, he won't give extensions. Nice guy at first. Don't try to take notes during class either. He switches slides back and fourth every 10 seconds.

analysis.name: Silvia Ferreira
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor was great in enhancing and supporting each student. Made the class feel more at home and laid back while still learning and enhancing writing skills. Readings may be a bit long but not too bad as they actually help you. There are 2 writing projects which she gives lots of time for and project builders to ease the process. Great Feedback!

One of the easiest classes I've taken. The professor is great, very accessible, accommodating, and a very lenient grader. There's a decent amount of reading, but overall it's manageable and not too time consuming. Would 100% recommend.

She is a nice person who tries to be accommodating. However, I took her BIS 164 class and all of the books were depressing. It was very clear they were selected to push political messages rather than show and appreciate the writers' skills. If you want an easy 4.0 take this. If you want to discover interesting and unique literature, you'll be sad.

Overall a good professor, though can get sort of monotone and repetitive at times. A lot of freedom given  to students for the overarching project. Much of the class can be lecture heavy with a couple activities sprinkled through, though when it is lecture, the content is often repeated 3-4 times in different ways through the class.
Very nice teacher, work was easy, there are daily in class activites you need to do with people but it's pretty easy. She's so enthusiastic makes class not feel dreadful and boring.

analysis.name: Erika Parsons
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Man.. she's a really nice person, but her teaching is intolerable. Her lectures are completely scattered and unfocused which makes it really hard to learn from class. Additionally, it seems that when she is unsure about an answer to a question, she defaults to asking the class.. and somehow the right answer is never established. Tough class to in..

Awful lectures. Not organized. Hard to follow because lack of visual aids. Discussion based classes not useful because Dr. Parsons will ask that we discuss in small groups topics we have only just been lectured on five minutes ago to "come up with answers on our own".  Not allowed to draw any pictures or diagrams on cheat sheet  for exams.
Don't waste your money to take her class. If you take you will regret!

Lectures are confusing, encourages students to answer each other's questions even though they may be wildly incorrect and ensures more confusion. Very difficult to succeed without putting a disproportionate amount of effort in.

Parsons is usually very unclear with instructions on the homework and exams. If you ask her questions over confusion with what she wants, she gives you the "if you don't understand it, that's your fault"type attitude. That sounds very unprofessional and I thought it's a professor's job to make sure students are understanding the stuff correctly.

analysis.name: Tracy Fields
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very easy and nice proffessor. Lots of the lectures are pretty boring because talking about climate change on a powerpoint isnt the most exciting but you were in groups a lot and makes class go by quicker. So much extra credit. I honestly dont even know how you could fail this class, just show up and do the assignments. Shes an easy grader.

Not great, not terrible. Lectures aren't the best so I stacked up on the in-class worksheets for extra credit. final project was easy, quiz every week or two, canvas assignments weekly also. TAKE NOTES while she's lecturing, and read the textbook. GO TO CLASS for extra credit!! like a 6/10 class overall tho.

I really enjoyed Professor Fields' lecture, despite it being long. As long as you take good notes and study the material, you will succeed in this class. I would absolutely take another class with her again, as she is very knowledgeable in her field and always answers questions thoroughly

analysis.name: Munehiro Fukuda
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Best computer science teacher, I've had so far! He's extremely organized, and gives class exercises to help learn the tough material. He notices if you're not in class and actually cares if you're successful or not. A bit hard to hear, so sit up front!

He encourages participation with in-class discussions that are actually helpful for understanding course material. He also gives hints to homework and exams if you attend lectures. Finally, you can ask questions and he will give useful answers. My biggest complaint is that, even when I sat in the front and he had a mic, I could barely hear him.

W professor who knows his stuff, and if you are into this field of work, then you will love him. If you just care about passing 430, there are probably easier professors. Participation is graded, hw is light, exams are tough, no extra credit, and lectures can sometimes get hard to follow due to pacing and sound (Japanese accent + directional mic).

Was very diligent and lax grading, offered a lot of extra credit opportunities and gave very clear feedback. If you were unsure about your grade, he gives up to a week to talk to him about it and get a grade change.

Going into the class, reviews made me skeptical, but after actually taking his class he has really grown on me. The material is not easy, and no matter how good his lectures are the programs/exams will still be tough. He provides recordings of his lectures which help tremendously. One of my favorite professors so far.

analysis.name: Frederick Douglass Alcorn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Alcorn is a very kind and funny person, but just extremely confusing when it comes to teaching. His assignments aren't clear at all, and he often rambles in class forever about useless things. The assignments aren't too difficult, and you have weeks to complete them, but they could just be more understandable

Phenomenal professor... he is funny, caring, & understanding. His assignments aren't clear, but he is open to explaining them, and he also gives a lot of extra credit. Such an interesting guy and his course was very enlightening, I loved it.

He's an easy grader as long as you do the work how he prefers. He really cares about quality over quantity. So he's flexible with deadlines if you need time. Throughout the quarter, there are only 4-6 assignments and a group project. You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches, but be patient with him, as he's not the best with tech.

He is so passionate about what he teaches and I loved his class. One of the best parts of my freshman year! But I understand why other people might not like him. My best advice is to talk during class, and stay after class to ask questions. I noticed that I would get higher grades on assignments as opposed to students next to me who stayed quiet.

I will admit that Prof Alcorn can be disorganized at times, but he is very passionate about what he teaches. He invites the class to discuss in dialogue, which I think is why sometimes the class may feel like it lacks structure. But he knows his stuff and you can learn a lot from him. He's also funny and definitely has some interesting life stories

analysis.name: Alejandro Francetich
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I love this prof!! He is super nice and open to help all his students. If you have questions on the exam he will help you if you talk to him. Only assignments were homework, in class problems and the exams and the exams are similar to the homework. Lectures were sometimes confusing but if you show up to class you will do well. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!

By far the easiest class I have ever seen. He is an extremely nice grader, as long as you participate he will like you. There was 4 homeworks and only 3 are graded. I turned them in late and got full credit still. The concepts of the class were very interesting but lectures can get a bit repetitive and boring. Participation is 1 minute reflections.

He is such a caring professor. Attending his class is mandatory because he has a graded exercise every day. His homework is very clear and his grading criteria is also very clear. It is a tough class but he is a very good professor. Highly recommend.

Great professor!! This class was interesting but with the wrong professor could be boring. With Francetich though the class was easy to understand, he gives thoughtful explanations and always has a smile on his face! Only a few homework's throughout the whole thing and the final is easy!

Ignore the course I chose, I had him for BCORE107 and he's genuinely a really nice guy who will give feedback and help if you ask. Only reason I rated him a 4 is because his lectures can feel a little heavy and often over-explained. Overall, a good professor.

analysis.name: Kivalina Grove
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
What's up with these bad ratings?? Dr. Grove is excellent, and her lectures are clear, informative, and fun. She cares for students and ensures that everyone is able to complete their work and succeed in her class. The exam is "hard" because some students think that having notes means having answers. 
One of the best professors I've had at UWB.

I ended up dropping the course because I did not learn much from it. Most lectures were mainly her reading off the PowerPoint slides, so it often felt like class time was not very useful. After the midterm, when the class average was around 58%, a lot of students started skipping, which reflected how disengaged people had become.

Lectures are alright. Very boring and no purpose to show up for as half the class doesn't. Group project was fun and easy until you saw your grade even when you put days of effort. Midterm and final are very hard as it's ABCDE format and one answer can have infinite meanings. Will not take again.

She speaks very quickly during lectures, which can make it difficult to keep up. She is somewhat nice that's about it. The exams and quizzes were much much more challenging than expected, especially for an introductory marketing course, and the class average remained relatively low.

Super Harsh grader, not an easy class. Other students taking the same course with a different teacher, learned more, and got better grades. Material Overall is easy. The questions are weird on the exams and quizzes, a question could have multiple answers, even though only one is right.

analysis.name: Gliboff Matthew
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you ever get a chance to take physics with him, do it.  He is always in class early, explains things very clearly, gives reasonable assignments and reasonable grades.  I wish I had taken him for the other two physics classes.
I like when you count homework more than exams

I had him for Physics 121 lab and Physics 123 lecture and lab. I dislike the class organization because it is built around "learning from your peers" and daily group work. A lot of the time your peers don't know what they are doing and it makes it difficult. He is a fair grader, but he doesn't grade anything himself, which is frustrating.

I think people forget that this class is offered as a quiz section, and not as a lecture. The literal point of the class is that we come in to work on the course content rather than receive a lecture based class. Professor Gliboff is great and really lenient, which really helps the workload. If you want to access a lecture he literally posts them.

He is prob one of the worst profs at UWB. Dosen't teach any of the material, we learn from the textbook and youtube videos. Somehow expects us to know what we are doing? Only meet once a week and yet we still get out early because we dont actually do anything in class except for "work" on problems. He is also lowk rlly sassy.

analysis.name: Tina Gourd
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tina is amazing. Very well organized, very knowledgeable, great individual feedback. Took her classes online and despite me not liking online classes much typically, hers were consistently engaging, interesting, and fun. So happy I had her, one of my favorite professors ever.

She is super organized & her lectures are really engaging. You're asked to discuss interesting questions w/ your table members frequently. I didn't really read anything but they're easy to skim for HW which is fairly decent & not hard, just writing assignments, no tests. Participation & attendance dictate your grade but it's well worth it.

Shes a good person and all, but not a good professor. Her instructions are really confusing and she gets scatter brained frequently. On the flip side shes very helpful one on one and gives very in depth feed back on your work. Her feedback is the best Ive gotten from any professor at UWB, but she should work on her public speaking.

analysis.name: Brandon Fleming
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 97 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He assigns a lot of reading and writing. Small assignments are graded nicely, but he takes away points on essays/projects for almost no reason. Very nice professor, but lectures are boring and he's impossible to reach outside of class.

idk why hes rated so highly...his instructions for essays are vague and he grades tough. and his canvas is hard to navigate. attendence is required but the lectures feel SO long because its so boring. hes got a very monotone none engaging tone that makes it hard to stay paying attention

I have taken Prof Fleming's class' for multiple courses. He is amazing although the work can be a lot at times his lectures are interactive he is kind and gives real world experience. His grading is great for learning it is easy to do well in this class as long as you show up and keep up and do your best! Best professor at UWB I have had.

He takes off points for things not in the rubric. He took off points for my final product pitch cuz it was not 3 mins long , though the directions said it has to be "max 3 mins", which literally 3 mins OR LESS. Brandon if you're reading this, please fix your grading and be fair when your directions contradict the complaints you have when scoring.

Professor doesn't know what he's talking about, spends too much time talking about himself/his previous ventures instead of actual material. Lectures are mandatory so you have to show up and hear him yap about whatever he wants. He isn't clear about directions and complains for small mistakes you make that the rubric didn't mention. Don't take him!

analysis.name: Gavin Doyle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Gavin is super funny, kind, and caring. He does a lot of group projects, but theyre graded on personal effort rather than the final product. a lot of the grades are participation-based, so dont miss class. For papers, he grades more heavily on the rough draft. And his written exams are essay-heavy (but he lets you pick which question to answer)

Gavin grades your drafts rough to squeeze as much effort out of you but goes easy on your final work. he knows not everyone believes they are talented at first and will grade you based on effort. Gavin also likes to get involved in projects and is upfront and honest about his work. I've taken him twice and he never fails to impress me.

Such a great prof. I couldn't go, but he held a movie night for fun. There was a film and short stories to read each week, but all he asked was that you annotate them with your opinions, so totally manageable. Final project was making a short film. Final exam was skippable if you did well on midterm and kept up on readings. Great experience overall

What I like about him is that he's super-flexible. You can blow 4 deadlines to do them later (he calls them resurrection tokens). I didn't notice it in the syllabus until later, but he has "exam bomb protection" built in where a high grade on weekly stuff will pull up your score after getting low exam scores. Anyway, he works to keep your GPA up.

Professor Doyle is a great professor, but as a BCORE class, I would say not to take. There are 2-3 readings a week and 1-2 films to watch as well, along with a midterm, a final exam (that can be skipped if you do well on the midterm), a research paper, and a short horror film you make as a group. Lots of work for a BCORE class, but great prof.

analysis.name: Mahmoud Ghofrani
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lecture style is focused for students who excels in understanding of circuit analysis. He will not provide extra nor detailed explanations during class for those who have difficulty absorbing new information, but rather move on with the lecture. Quality of instructor heavily depends on exam average, and he hardly reaches above 80.

I loved Dr. Ghofrani's classes! He explained things very thoroughly and gave numerous practice problems for us to work on prior to tests. His tests were very straightforward, as long as you'd practiced the homework problems and his midterm/final lecture slides, you would've performed very well. He is also very nice about accepting late work.

BE READY, because this lecturer will expect you to know Differential Eq. and provide no background explanation. Students must have comprehensive understanding of circuit analysis because exam problems will NOT be similar to any problems from lectures, quiz, HW, and exam reviews. Class is basically "The Great Filter" for EE students. Exam Avg : 70%
So goated. Recorded lectures, homeworks arent too hard, exams arent too hard either. I actually understood a lot when i took him and it helps a lot in EE 200. Def take him

Ghofrani is just great. He solves all the problems on the board. Lectures are very helpful for homework. The exams are just like the homework and practice problems he has posted. Before each exam, he has a review session, which is very helpful. He really cares for his students.

analysis.name: Maryam Griffin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Shes not a lawyer which makes sense once you take her class. I initially thought she was in the wrong room. BIS 283 (Intro to Law) with Maryam is less about law and more about her showing off her PHD in Sociology. The class is largely graded based on a final group project. Boring class. Not a lot of learning. I blame UWB for the failure.

As a woman, I found it offensive when she claimed that she cares about the plight of minorities. She has no life experience to back up that claim. Simply put, she is a phony. She told me that she barely passed law school. SOC is all she had to save face. She has my sympathy.
super easy A and easy class. Homework is just reading LONG articles and answering questions. lectures were a little boring as it was just her rambling for hours.
Great professor. This class was very manageable as long as you kept up with the assignments. If you followed the instructions and completed the work on time, it was very possible to earn full points.
So nice!!! Take her if you can.

analysis.name: Gani Nurmukhametov
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Solid professor, had him for BDATA200. PICK YOUR GROUP WISELY! A lot of your points is on group projects so make sure you have a solid group or you will be annoyed. No midterms/no finals - just group projects only, a couple in class assignments (easy), has LinkedIn Learning assignments that are so long, but easy. Overall good class.

Professor is clearly passionate about economics and math, often working through a problem multiple times in class to make the answer clear for everyone. Allows opportunities to discuss and keeps his class engaged. Almost everyone in the class came to class despite it not being a requirement. Overall, definitely one of the best professors at UW.

Clearly is passionate about what he is teaching and truly wants every single one of his students to succeed. Workload was not too time consuming at all. Notes are your best friend. There are 5 problem sets to be worked through with a group you are given at the beginning of the quarter and 2 exams (not bad as long as you study).

Best professor hands down. Gani explained concepts super well, was patient and allowed for questions, and made microeconomics an enjoyable class. If you attend class, take notes, and do you work you will get a good grade. I wish I could take him for macroeconomics.

Professor Gani has been one of my favorite professors at Bothell. As long as you go to class and listen, you will be able to get a good score. Even if you don't (like I did towards the end), if you shoot him an email, he can perfectly explain your questions, and you can tell he actually cares about his students and them doing well in his class.

analysis.name: Laura  Harkewicz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Harkewicz is one of the rudest teachers I've taken. She would respond in snarky and demeaning ways when asked questions by the class. Also, I didn't realize this was a writing class, because she solely grades on writing skills. If your work doesn't match her answer exactly written in impeccable form, expect a low grade

Lectures tend to drag, and the way she engages with students in discussions is imo a little intense and condescending. But the workload is super light, just a couple (very interesting) readings and one writing assignment a week, sometimes a quiz. If you follow the instructions it's easy to get full points. Overall easy A.

BIS380 was an easy class. Professor looking for ways to take off points, she is a tough grader. Do not rely only on chatGPT or AI you need to read the assignments & give good answers for full credit. Assignment heavy class tbh, midterm was online and final is online too. She's overall okay!

There are some assignments which you can't just wing, and the Professor will deduct points if you did not address all points mentioned in a reading. Seems to grade reading responses harsher than actual papers. Accommodates appropriately for mishaps like cyclones, and will remove assignments if needed- compared to some professors >:(.

I was not a fan of how she would teach. When she tries to create a discussion, it would feel like our answers would be wrong. Her "lectures" tend to go on and on and she tends to forget what she was saying. There is also a LOT of reading in this class. Her guidelines are not clear whatsoever for the major assignments.

analysis.name: Zade Himanshu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Doesn't answer emails, unprepared & awkward lectures, and rude
I believe this class was a waste of time, you don't learn anything new from 360 and he would often ask us if we did a certain subject in 360, he's the professor, he should know! 
He would call you out in class saying your question or answer was wrong (his feedback would make no sense)

No exams at all and the whole class is pretty much team based. His grading criteria is kind of wack but honestly his grading isnt super harsh, for example he never deducts points for late work. Just super boring lectures

I had him for 360 last year and now 444. His lectures can get long and dry after a while, but otherwise he's a very passionate professor and you can tell he enjoys the subjects he teaches. He's lenient on homework deadlines, especially if you reach out, and there are no tests. Would highly recommend taking him for any course.

analysis.name: David Goldstein
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The grading system is very, very weird. It would be better if he just did a traditional grading system. Some films are interesting, some are not. The TA does all the grading, which kind of made me feel as if he doesn't participate in the class. Key for getting a good grade: REVISE! Revising the essays is the best way to get the maximum grade.

The class itself is not extremely difficult, he's weird grading system is. He doesn't believe in traditional grading so he came up with his own unique one. In my opinion it is poop because he will not let you know your grade until the end of the quarter. Throughout this whole quarter my course grade as been locked so I have no idea if I am passing

This is the second class that I have taken from Professor Goldstein. On a usual week, there is a documentary to watch, which is followed by a discussion board. I personally really like his mastery grading system because he allows revisions for big assignments. This class is an easy 4.0 if you do the work on time.

Really odd grading style that makes it hard to receive an A. If your taking it because you think its an easy A, its not. Majority of grade comes from 2 assignments and you won't even know your final grade until the end of the class. Dont bother emailing either he doesn't respond :)

David is a nice person, but not one of the more impressive profs I've had at UW. His instructions are detailed to the point of being confusing and overly complicated. He let class out early every day, which gave me the impression that he was not interested in lecturing or getting deeper into discussion.

analysis.name: William Hartmann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Even though I got an A, this professor made it difficult to understand assignments. He is a good man, but his grading and assignments are the issues, not him. It seems as though he skims papers, and barely gives feedback.

I will say, I respect him as a man and a father, but never as a professor. 

Sorry, sir. But try better next time.

The essays were graded in a way that no one was able to get full points. It feels almost impossible to get a 4.0. Every time someone asked him a question he'd respond by asking the class what they thought, except the class never knew, so the questions would be left unanswered. I regret taking this class & will be avoiding his future classes.

His lectures are boring and hard to focus on. You barely get enough time to work on the essays, his deadlines are too short, assignments feel last minute, and his planning seems unorganized. He claims the essays are based on interpretations but then marks it as missing details that he doesn't elaborate on what we need to do to improve them.

great professor!!! explained things so clearly and used the board a lot (which is great for me). he was receptive to raised hands and really took time to break questions down and give alternative examples and stuff. i was lowkey late to every class and i still feel like i learned a lot. hartmann ftw!!!

I didnt enjoy this class much, I wanted more hands on work. His lectures got boring, he just talks and talks. But he plans very well. Book is required for the 10 question quiz that is open book and be taken at home. I liked this class because there was no midterm or final. go to class everyday, he has little class activities that are a few points.

analysis.name: Susan Harewood
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I'll be honest, most negative comments come from students who don't put in effort. Yes, there is a lot of reading and writing, but this is a 490-level class. If you attend, participate, and try, you'll do well. She grades fairly and creates space for open discussion and debate, which is rare today. Expect to work hard, learn deeply, and grow a lot!

I am utterly DISAPPOINTED in this professor. The amount of work she gives out is unbelievable, with 2 papers due per week ALONG with additional assignments and 2 hours of documentary watching. This class has kept me from effectively completing the work of my other classes.

This was hands down the worst experience/class I have ever taken. Her expectations were ridiculous & her grading criteria was insane! The topics she teaches sound interesting but she ruins it for students by overworking them until they are completely burned out & no longer engaged. She is known to hand out failing grades to good students. RUN!!
Mark my words, the course load is absolutely inhuman! Tough grader: completely inconsistent and unpredictable as well.  Avoid like the plague!

Goated professor.

He gets straight to the point and takes his time making sure we understand the material. He's also a very easy lenient grader and is passionate in teaching. Homework is often due every 2 weeks so you have lots of time to complete it. Drops one midterm and also adds 25 extra points if you turn in your hw on time. Had fun learning in his class!

He is easily the best professor I have had in my few years of college, the reason the difficulty is a 2 and not higher is because of how well he teaches, if you have questions or don't understand something, he is genuinely excited to teach you so its comforting. Great person, great teacher, if you have the opportunity to take his class, please do.

I don't think I have a words of how great of a math professor he is. I swear if he was my math professor for the rest the time I am in college, I'd practically be going to heaven. I have never met a better professor than him. It's unfortunate that he doesn't teach calc 2 or 3 I really wish he did.

It's like finding a needle in a haystack. I'm so lucky to have this math professor over any of the others. It's so refreshing and heart-warming to have such a great professor for math. analysis.name: Rania Hussein

Dr. Hussein is an incredible professor and really cares about her students. Her lectures closely apply to the assignments and are engaging, and the labs are challenging but fun. You will learn a lot of material that can be used in future careers.
She is great!. I learned a lot about embedded systems, C programming and operating systems in this course and feel confident in my skills. Definitely a worthwhile experience.

Dr. Hussein is the best professor that the UWB EE faculty has EVER had the privilege of having. Dr. Hussein is one of my favorite professors at UWB. I have taken 271, 332, and 425 with her & loved all of her classes. She makes sure you understands everything and value your hard work. She is not only a good lecturer but also amazing during lab.

analysis.name: Thomas Humphries

Dr. Humphries taught Matrix Algebra with great clarity and intuitiveness. I am so glad he came to UWB. The averages on the tests and the homework where high Bs, but mostly due to the dedicated nature of the students. That said, introductory matrix algebra is easy, either made easy by Dr. Humphries or easy by nature. I strongly recommend.

He is one of the best STEM professors at UW Bothell, all his assignments have nice deadlines usually one week, the study guide is almost the same thing as the test, he just changes the numbers and some of the wording, he also gives a front and back cheat sheet that you can use, getting a good grade in this class shouldn't be that hard.
He's a great professor who wants students to succeed. I wish I were a better student but this was a phenomenal class, one of the best I've taken at UWB

He wants people to learn. He is kind, and makes a hard subject easier to digest. The class still presents its challenges, but is way more manageable with this prof. I recommend asking him for help with any questions you may have about assignments. He provides study guides and office hours.

i really liked her! she was very clear on assignment guidelines and always responded to emails quick. she also held conferences with us, which actually really helped and i think i grew as a writer! i didn't like how it was 100/0%, but you could revise to get credit (i didn't need to do this - she was pretty lenient and understanding for grading).
Does not listen to students what so ever. Thinks she is so much better than she is and does not care about your work even if you try your best. Gives out so much homework just to not grade it.

I have taken two courses with her and her classes are super well put together, interesting, lots of variety in subject and assignments, fun, and she is very organized and clear with expectations and instruction. Professor Demir is a really sweet guy and really cares for our learning. Every assignment in this class is all assisted by him, and so you can get help on literally anything, and he will respond and help. Highly recommend him for any business or economics course you won't regret!

analysis.name: Jason Lambacher

analysis.name: Jonathan Lee
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

One big final paper due at the end of the quarter (hard). He does not give clear instructions on basically anything so ask him lots of questions. He is very kind and approachable

analysis.name: Jeff Jensen

exams hard af, study guides make me feel like im cramming the whole textbook for one exam
bro is terrible, very unorganized no actual study exam prep.
