Halway through the quarter somone cheated on our midterm so she punished all of us and voided the midterm for everyone which made our final worth double. 10 minutes before the test started, she changed the format again so everything we had studied for no longer mattered.

Her schedule for tests and projects became very disorganized and hectic. Project guidelines were unclear at times and tests became different than what was previously stated. Her TA grades and heavy work for everything she is supposed to do. She failed me as a professor, and lacked basic communication to set us up for success. AVOID HER ASAP!

analysis.name: Clark Olson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He teaches as though he doesn't care at all about whether or not the student learns and only offers his way of looking at problems, leading to narrow, confusing explanations. Office hours are no better. If you have to take his class for the Grad Certificate, just live with it I guess. But if you have a chance to avoid him, do it.

I learned a lot from the programming assignments, dealing with image processing, but I was expecting more from the lectures. He seemed to want to put the onus on us to learn the material on our own, and then spend lecture time answering our questions, and the like. Also, his weekly notes did not jibe well with the textbook.
he is very knowlegable but clearly havign hardtime communicating his knowledge and his feedbacks to students. he cares about learning but his lectures are too deviated from the book.

find yourself doing a lot of homework with not much value added work. feedback from homeworks are generally discouraging. materials are sometimes confusing with typos. his mid-term can be tough or easy be prepared for a surprise. he is generous with grading usually after a tough test. no extra credit. he acctually spends time to catch cheating.

I took his vision class and learned close nothing. Assignments were very very easy. Lectures were informal and had no math in them (vision is very math-heavy area). Project was a figment. May be it's because it is Bothell campus? Don't know. But just don't waste your time.

analysis.name: Osama Hamdan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Osama is a awesome professor! super laid back and chill. Works in the field (microsoft and google) while being a adjunct professor so he uses real life scenarios in his explanations. His lectures are really easy to follow and understand. Tests are easy and he helps you get prepared for them. Easy homework assignments. A real gem at UWB!

This class is the easiest 370 on campus, and you will get an A, but it is a bit of a waste of time as you won't really learn much. Class was routinely cut an hour short. Osama is really nice and insanely helpful as he does this for a living for big companies, it's just a bit too easy. Would recommend if taken with hard classes. No midterm or final!

*Actually for CSS370*
Appriciate not having to go to class and basically buy in my 5 credits with little effort. All his material is stolen from another professor and doesn't set up his Canvas correctly. Lectures are ~30 mins long reiterating the stolen readings.
Only take if you just want the credits and don't want to learn anything.

Professor Hamdan is a wonderful professor that does a great job teaching CSS 370 by applying his relevant knowledge in the tech industry and exposing its realities based on his experience towards its students. Not many professors for 370 have a background like him, so take him and you won't regret it!

(CSS370) May Allah bless this man most graciously ameen. Best prof I have taken at UWB, doesn't waste time with long lectures or assignments. Grading is as straightforward as it gets. Focuses on applicability from his job at a big FAANG company

analysis.name: Gunwha Oh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall, Professor Oh is very sweet and kind. She often provides decent lectures that provide lots of useful information for your labs and homework assignments. She is very responsive to emails and is very approachable for extra help. Beginning of the quarter focuses more on concepts, while the end focuses heavily on coding. Favorite GIS course.

The course was lecture heavy and super dense in terms of topic load but Oh is a very kind professor who remembered past students and was very responsive when I emailed with code issues. The midterm was incredibly difficult (took me 8 hours to complete) and I got a pretty low score but she let us do extra credit and I ended up with over 100% on it.

Although shes a respected teacher, it is extremely difficult to learn in her class. Most of the work is labs which consist of making maps using ArcGIS. There is minimal explanation on how to actually use the software. You are expected to learn yourself. Accent is also heavy which makes it difficult to understand lectures. Hard grader as well.

She is very sweet and kind, but the class is not great. There are weekly quizzes, and you don't learn everything you need to in order to do well. You have do do a lot of outside research in order to answer some of the questions. You don't really need to go to class cause the lectures aren't helpful anyway. Lab sections are great though.

This class was awesome because of how hands-on it was - I learned the most from the labs, which were quite a bit of work. A lot of really important stuff is covered in the lectures, and while her accent makes it harder to understand her, she explains things in pretty simple terms which helps.

analysis.name: Pietro Paparella
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I have taken classes with nearly every mathematics instructor at UWB, and Paparella is easily one of, if not THE, best one. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, take it. I only wish that he had been hired earlier so that I could've taken more of his classes.

Really chill guy. Lectures go much more in depth than textbook/homework, but sometimes it felt like he was complicating the content a bit, so it was a little hard to follow. Exams (2 midterms + final) are exactly like the practice ones, which are very straightforward. Matlab homework after every lecture. Also, he's kinda a hottie

Pietro is a very good instructor. He's very clear about what he expects from you and assigns take home assignments and tests which are hard if you don't do the homework. We had to do some proofs for this class, so expect them on the exams. Linear algebra is not easy so reading the textbook is sometimes necessary as Pietro moves in a fast-pace.

Before anything, I would like to say that I took STMATH 427 with Professor Paparella, but it did not have the option.

Professor Paparella really cares that the students understand the course material as opposed to anything else, and that makes it really easy to engage in his course. Quizzes and problem sets should be obvious if you pay attention.

Pretty chill class. You don't have to show up to lecture unless it's a quiz day, but I would recommend it. Quizes are easy but, make sure you show your work clearly I got docked a ton of points for the first two weeks. Homework takes 1-2 hours and exam models the practice tests. Professor cares about the students, and easy to reschedule quizes.

analysis.name: Hyung Oh
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He gets right to the point. Probably one of the best professors ive had. His tests are short and does not take the full 2 hours, and there are extra credit questions on them to. Be aware, getting above a hundred percent only gives you a hundred percent (not 109). Homework is short. He sometimes teaches us stuff not relevant, but still interesting!

This was his first time teaching and i think he did great. He makes sure to clarify everything you don't understand and tries to have everyone in class up to pace. He sometimes speaks nonsense but it is hilarious. He is a lenient grader. His tests are short but worth a lot question. As long as you understand the HW from the book you will be okay.

I think he is a great teacher. It was his first year teaching and he makes sure to have everyone up to pace. He clarifies everything you don't understand. Sometimes he speaks nonsense but it is hilarious. I think he uses time efficiently and the tests are short but worth a lot. As long as you understand the material from the HW then you are good.

A great professor who cares and wants you to understand the basics rather than just memorize them. No reading required because everything on the test in from lecture. If you don't understand something he will explain it as many ways as he can and if you fail it really is because you didn't put any effort into the course. Gives extra credit too!

Dr. Oh is awesome. He is funny and tries his best to teach students that accounting is "fun and useful". The course consists of ten HW assignments and three exams (2 midterms, 1 final). The homework was graded very easily.. I only missed 1 point. The exams are straight-forward and questions come from homework/review q's. Extra credit on exams!

analysis.name: Douglas Pyle
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class felt kinda pointless and business centric group projects for almost every homework assignment. Professor was nice but didn't really feel like he was prepared for a group project class, doesn't enforce or provide much support for group members who don't participate or issues with groups. Overall very nice but not a good prof for group work!

Lots of assignments felt like busy work. Randomly selected group projects with a lot of assignments feeling 75% similar to the last one. Lots of assignments require 2 pages of writing. The quizzes are online and outside of class time, not too bad. So many random busy work assignments though.

I took CSS350 with him not CSS110. Proffesor Pyle was hands down my best professor, he truly cared for student success and this class was super easy. Online quizzes no midterms or finals and best of all, he brought amazing fun snacks for us everyday. 10/10 oh and great lectures

Quizzes every week based on readings, super easy and usually knew by memory. Doug is really nice, chill, and easy to work with, had an extensive background with big tech companies. Mid-term was closed note and was the one that stumped most. Studying extra hard for the midterm payed off, but the average was low result in an open note online final.

His class had weekly open-note quizzes and biweekly homework, which was easy with high averages. The professor seemed decently knowledgeable about Cybersecurity but was often caught off guard by questions. However, the one midterm stumped the majority of the class, and the class didn't adequately prepare students for it resulting in an online final

analysis.name: Peng Du
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ignore the guy that gave Peng a 1.0. I think I know who he is and he was a bad student. Peng isn't perfect but he gets close to it. His tests are hard and weighted heavily like all coding classes. Studying for them is easy, he records his lectures and bases his tests off his lectures.

Professor Du is the best CS professor ever!! Whatever class he's teaching that quarter, take it. His lectures and code alongs are engaging, homework and exams are reasonable, and he's always available to help you on discord even if it's late. He makes difficult concepts simple to understand. Seriously do not hesitate to take him!!!

TL;DR: Prof. Peng is fantastic. Just go to class, code along, and you'll be fine. As a business major, I didn't expect to get so much out of a CS course. Beyond Java, I learned real interview tips, practiced Git commands, and learned how to write solid code. He's easy to reach &always open to chat, which made the class both practical and enjoyable.

AMAZING professor. This was my first time taking summer classes and I only did it so I could take Peng for CSS 143 because I have heard from other students how he gives very good lectures and is a great professor. They were all right. He is so understanding and amazing at his job. I heavily recommend taking him if you can. Lots of Extra credit!!

Professor Peng has to be one of the best professors at uwb especially within the CSSE department, he uses practical examples and simplifies content which caters to each students learning. He is also active on discord even at 12am which makes contacting him super easy. His grading policy is niceas he wants students to learn and worry less on grades.

analysis.name: Yusuf Pisan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's an awesome dude, and really cares about what he's teaching, not super great with feedback on the assignments and sometimes expects you to know material that he hasn't taught yet. Grade is extremely test heavy and the tests are way harder than the assignments. This class was time consuming and his lecture's weren't always helpful.

Super nice guy, but did not teach Operating Systems very well. Heavily relied on outdated slides from the textbook which at times were out of order, had vague, conflicting, or even MISSING information. Reading the textbook was a pain as the author would go off on tangents for several pages at a time. Prepare to heavily use StackOverFlow/YouTube.

Quiz takes up 20% of the whole grade. It is a game development class and half of the quiz are on history of games. Watch Youtube tutorials on Unity; it is where youll learn the most out of this class. Read the book to find out why past game developers are important and what are their contribution, and the rest you can get from the lecture slides.

Doesn't teach well. He assumes that everyone in the class is in the same pace or level of knowledge, thus this class will favor those who likes programming or majoring in CS. And most importantly, the weekly homework are tough as hell. Exams aren't that tough as the HW, but points are easily deducted because he is a strict and tough grader.

Organized relative to other professors, but assigns a lot of work. Quarter-long group project based on a Unity game, but hard to finish if never used Unity before and only 10 weeks. Often gives unclear instructions or makes mistakes regarding assignments, and is unresponsive until the next class after when it is due. Can be mean sometimes.

analysis.name: Madhu Rajanna
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Look, I agree that this class was not organized and maybe could have been handled better, but if you take Professor Rajanna, you will be met with someone who genuinely cares about you as a student, is always offering extensions, goes out of their way to make sure you learn (but you need to go out of your way and ask for help), etc. Loved CSS478.

Madhu is a pretty chill guy. If you go to his lectures, he does try to make students participate as he tries to make it interactive. The more people participate, it actually gets the ball rolling and he teaches really well. He's pretty nice and enthusiastic about teaching. If you show him enthusiasm and participate, the class is actually p fun.

Professor seemed pretty knowledgable on the subject, but not how to teach. He was not great at interacting with the students, answering the questions, or helping you if you fell behind. I'd highly recommend a different professor.

This class probably shouldn't be offered in its current manner. It's about a week or two's worth of content stretched out over 10 weeks. Professor is nice and he does a good job of explaining things. Quizzes and exams are embarrassingly easy and the class is so easy it makes you feel bad for taking it. Course Canvas is badly set-up, though.

This was Professor Rajanna first time teaching BIMD233, and yes it was obvious but he was always willing to help and answer questions if needed. The grading did take forever, but that was more on his grader. As long as you attend the lectures and ask questions!! you will succeed in this course.

analysis.name: Padilla Amparo Yolanda
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Padilla is an awesome and passionate professor who is always engaged with the class. The assignments are easy if you follow the rubric, but the workload is extremely heavy. This was by far my most stressful class, mainly because of the amount of reading on top of the actual assignments. She's extremely slow at grading assignments.

Dr Padilla is a very kinda and compassionate professor who is extremely passionate about Ethnic studies. I have take two courses with her, both had weekly readings with a midterm and final, alongside a final paper. Her course can be alot if you struggle with readings. However, by participating in class and doing the readings, she will reward you.

Professor Padilla was very passionate about the topic and explained things in ways that made sense. You do have to show up to class and do the homework/readings in order to understand what is going on. The more effort you put in the more you will get out of the class.

Overall, if you do your work on time and participate, this is an easy class. The assignments can be a bit tedious, but doable. She's very attentive and kind, but willing to call on people at random if no one is participating.

Really nice, understanding and caring professor, I don't understand all the negative comments on here about her 'biases' because understanding and confronting history is not 'liberal'. She assigns a lot of work every week but it's doable. There is a final and a midterm, and an essay due at the end of the quarter.

analysis.name: Ron Krabill
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: genuinely one of the best classes i've taken at UWB. i took bismcs 333 and genuinely felt like i learned something. YAY seriously in my professor hall of fame. quarter long group project and weekly small group meetings, no quizzes but weekly assignments (250 word application of concepts, really easy if you did readings or paid attention in class)

Mr. Krabill is a great teacher. He is very engaging and cares about us as students. The coursework is light just some readings and discussion post. One group project and essay at the end of the quarter. Very chill but still very informative!

BISMCS33. Ron Krabill was honestly the first professor at UW Bothell that I have ever really liked. He was caring for his students and the class was discussion based which typically I hate but I found myself wanting to participate each time. If I was not graduating I would be taking Ron for any course possible!!!

I had high expectations going into this class and none were met.  He focuses too heavily on group work, and as most of us know, group work at UWB can be very painful.  Every class was led by students and the last 20 min Krabill would chime in.  I really feel like I missed out as Krabill is an extrememly smart man.  I wanted to hear from him more.

The class was about human rights issues; on average 30 pages of reading were assigned weekly. You will most likely meet a bunch of cynical Democrats who care nothing but "social justices" regardless of the reality. Cynicism caused by the media was never addressed in the class. Accusations without valid clues were made constantly.

analysis.name: Adam Romero
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took him in B Core 104 the class is super easy. He is a fun professor that cares about everyones grades. It is a very simple class and he pretty much walks you through the assignments and what to do in them. even though attendance isn't required I there are graded in class worksheets. The class is also very helpful for doing the HW.
This professor is amazing! He's easy to reach outside of class, has good humor during lectures, and is very reasonable and lenient with grading. Also there's quite a bit of reading in this class fyi

The course felt unfocused, with many AI-related questions that didn't seem relevant to the core material. I personally didn't gain much from the lectures and wouldn't recommend it if you're looking for structured learning. Tbh, it was wasting money.
Took B CORE 104, very light class. No tests/quizzes, just submit the homework questions and write the stories (I found them fun lol).

In class, he talks a lot for BCORE 104 about Utopian imagination. However, there are usually two assignments per week which are pretty easy and doesn't require much time. Basically graded on completion as well. Free 4.0 if you do the work on time and show at least a little effort in your work

analysis.name: Zak Rubin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: STAY AWAY. Course is poorly designed by another prof and all profs blindly follow it. Instructions, book, and rubric contradict each other. Grading is inconsistent. Questions are dismissed instead of clarified. Lectures go off track and don't help in class, though she shares valuable professional experience. Very hostile learning environment.

Don't penalize them for a poorly structured course (it's BAD, but they didn't design it). IMO they made the most of a bad situation as a new prof. Extremely accessible outside of class and has a lot of really valuable industry experience they're willing to share. Precise but fair. What some describe as rudeness I just took as them being direct.

Genuinely the best professor I've ever had, I always enjoy coming to class every week! Dr. Zak makes the most out of the curriculum while giving us a valuable learning experience. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She also gives out free energy drinks, and is easy to talk to if you need help or an extension.

The professor is unclear as the rubric and instructions consistently contradicted each other, and when asked for clarification, you're met with VERY RUDE responses. The only positive is that they review a couple of questions on the actual exam during class beforehand, + the questions on the final exam were very easy (more reflective than testing).

Nah. Very poor class design made by a different prof, and Zak clearly had no interest in the class itself. Often went on tangents and grading was wildly inconsistent. Snarky remarks to questions and was kind of rude. Lectures weren't *that* relevant to the work. You will leave this class with character development.

analysis.name: Rejoice Akapame
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor is a joke. all the class slides are AI generated nonsense, which she doesn't understand herself. Skips over almost everything, saying "you can figure that out". Is unable to provide explanations for how or why something is done, teaches straight from textbook. Exams are all online, but have too many problems to complete in time. BAD!

Don't take it if you want to learn statistics in depth - lectures just reiterate the book and its problems. If you learn well on your own and want a free high grade, then GO for it. Exams and HW are online, and you have all the materials you need to do well on them. The only negative for some will be weekly in-person quizzes and graded attendance.

Easily the worst teacher I've had in my 17 years of education.  Unprepared.  Does not know how to read the room.  Gives no feedback.  Seems unaware of reality.  And was absent on the day of our big project presentation to boot.  the irony, is the class was about how to be a good teacher, create a good curriculum, and give appropriate feedback. sad

I was in her calculus class and genuinely enjoyed it. Personally, I don't think I have had a professor who explained things so well especially a math course, but she was great. She gives step by step instructions and examples how to solve problems and uses real world situations as examples. Pay attention in class and you will pass.
Not a very engaging class. Test are all over the place. The class felt like a joke.

analysis.name: Raissa Desmet
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 121 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Raissa is a very nice person, not such a great professor, so unorganized, didn't let us know that a class was going to be on zoom, so people still showed up, wasted gas and time, very inconsiderate. Doesn't know how to use canvas ,idk?  But always issues with assignments, grading, posting announcements, and answering emails. Do not take her.

Dr Raissa is super caring and the most engaging lecturer I have had at UW Bothell. If you need or want to take a Global studies/Ethnic studies you wont regret taking her class. She approaches her topics with a perfect blend of seriousness, considering the issues she presents, paired with her comical and uplifting personality when appropriate.

Absolutely loved having Raissa as my prof for this quarter. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches, and it shows. Attendance was mandatory which made me groan at first, but I ended up looking forward to coming to class every week. She makes sure everyone chats with each other so that we can create a sense of community. LOVE HER.

I was not expecting to enjoy this class given that I just took it to fill in one of my higher-level elective requirements but Raissa made the class so enjoyable and engaging. Would love to take her again!

Nice lectures, bad person. She will give you some "hints" instead of telling you what you should do. Sometimes I feel she is chill but sometimes it is frustrating and confusing to fulfill her requirements. She is always polite and we respect her. But she will keep distances from students and seldom respond email until days later. Not recommend

analysis.name: Renukka Ahhuja
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Most valueless class and teacher. Expects us to self-learn everything. Never checks-in on us in class. Grade mostly based on a final with no learning checkpoints, expects us to be in class everyday just to sit around?!

You won't learn anything in class so it is very important you understand the homework and textbook. She gives vary vague instructions on group projects, then cold calls you when you miss something during the presentation. Very unorganized and "teaches" by reading over slides and calls it a day.
Very lenient and caring professor, lectures aren't super engaging but if you just want a passing grade this is a good bet.

Previous reviews have been deleted many times now. I believe she reports them and they are deleted. Probably the least caring professor I have ever had, classes are bland and disorganized and clearly isn't willing to take criticism.
The grade is based on class reflections, homework, a presentation, and the final. She is nice.

analysis.name: James Reinnoldt
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 172 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Yes, James is an lenient grader and his workload is manageable. However, he wasn't the nicest professor. He was very condescending. I don't like him
If you are considering taking his class, good luck!
Great class. Huge amount of work but very relevant. Learned so much. Project teams were a drag. He also really helps students prepare for career skills
Knows his stuff. Just listen and take good short notes that will help you on test. Be honest and enjoy his real world stories.

Professor Reinnoldt is incredible. Distinguished, intelligent, articulate and amusing. By far my favorite prof in the 2 years and a quarter at UW. His lectures are geared towards current events making it easy to connect the discipline. Everything you learn in this class will be used in the real world. Incredible story teller. Take him for anything.

analysis.name: Stephie Kang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Stephie is an amazing prof. She has a genuine passion to teach and can be clearly seen through her PowerPoints. I always appreciated her feedback and her "What's going on around campus" slides at the beginning of each class. She is so kind hearted and easy to follow.

An amazing professor. I highly recommend taking her class! 

She has a genuine passion for teaching and is incredibly kind and supportive. Her feedback on assignments is thoughtful and detailed.

Her grading is labor-based, so as long as you complete all the assignments, you should have no trouble earning a 4.0.
Classes are very simple, structured in a simple manner and she accommodates all students regardless of writing ability. If you show up to class and do homework you'll get an A.
Flexible to work with, nice professor, if you do the minimal grade you get an A-/A+

analysis.name: Scott Shippy
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One thing that made this lab so frustrating for me was the lab reports and not getting clear direction on it, most of the work you'd have to just look at the procedure and hope you did the Lab well. I am not the biggest fan on his grading especially since multiple students who have never done a lab report didnt do that well yet got graded bad.

My initial impression of Shippy was that he is an incredibly tough grader, but he makes up for that entirely by giving incredibly good feedback. I never scored below ~80% on any of the later labs due to the amount of constructive criticisms he writes on your lab reports. He is also incredibly easy-going in lab and has a fantastic sense of humor.

I genuinely dread going to this lab. There is an obvious difference between the way he treats the women in the class vs the men. Asking questions is usually a waste of time because he doesn't actually give you an answer, he beats around the bush and then tells you to basically figure it out yourself. This is a last resort lab, don't take it.

BCHEM144 is a required course for a lot of people and if you can take the other instructors of this course, do so. Don't take Shippy unless it really fits your schedule. He's ok as a lab instructor, but he's one of the harshest graders I had for lab reports. A few mistakes could set you up for a GPA killer of a course.

He is very condescending and talks down to people. He will never give you the answer to your question and will always  work around the question. He nitpicks every small detail on reports and even after improving on my next report, he will find something else to take away points from. Take another instructor if you can.

analysis.name: Todd Martinez-Simmons -Simmons
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great and chill professor. The assignments are fun and interactive, which is rare to see these days. The grading criteria is clear and straightforward. He also has a great sense of humor and is understanding. The class is flexible and not just focused on lectures; if you miss an in-class activity, he usually provides make-up assignments online.
Lots of busy work, and changed the final twice. Radio silent once finals week rolled around. Chill and fun professor in class, but the work and other difficulties were unpleasant.
Great professor, really passionate and funny. Loves the subject and it shows. Could improve feedback, but grades leniently as well.

analysis.name: Anurag Tewari
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Tewari is a great teacher. If you're ever confused about smth just ask him, he's always ready to help. The course uses excel, so learn a bit before the quarter starts. Exam questions were very similar to the hw so if you know how to do the hw you're good. There are a few graded workshops, so be sure not to miss those, and a short group project.

Professor Tewari is obviously passionate about what he teaches and wants students to understand. Sometimes his lectures are a bit fast but he always is wiling to explain further or go back. There were multiple opprotunities to improve your midterm grade which was very gracious. Show up to class-not mandatory but you will be confused if you don't.

He is very passionate & knowledgeable but sometimes sounds confusing. Using Pearson is crucial to success and playing around with excel before taking the class would be quite helpful to understand what he is saying. He's the best accounting prof I've ever had. He's very friendly helpful and caring about students. And he loves Costco so much. His exams are heavy but if you read textbooks/slides and study well it's possible to get A for this class. Homework is a lot and sometimes it is hard but he explains it in class. Must take his class!:)

analysis.name: Amaranth Borsuk
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is nice, but she and the other two professors who co-teach this course are very inexperienced. They have no idea how to properly grade assignments, so instead they give every student the same low grade. You need 54/54 points to get a 4.0, and they will take away points randomly, so don't take this thinking it will be an easy class.

I really enjoyed her class and she is a wonderful professor! Her mood really helped me open up and make friends. The class is a breeze and we do lots of arts & crafts; which is a nice break from coding.
Such a nice teacher, I loved her so much, her assignments were very easy, all we really did was crafts. The late work policy was great.

Professor Amaranth Borsuk is an easy grader. As long as you meet the criteria for a section of the rubric, you get full points for that section. Furthermore, the thresholds to get grades are low, so you can miss a few minor assignments and still get a 4.0. Beware of mandatory assignments, however.

Professor Amaranth is amazing! she was so accepting of everyone's literary works, never shaming anyone and always giving very meaningful comments on our submissions. Creates a respectful environment, especially when reviewing student poetry. This course is team-taught by her and one other prof. After week 4 they switch and week 5 is a "break" week.

analysis.name: Ambikar Rucha
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The readers that are assigned in this class are VERY long. She doesn't cover all of the topics in class, and likes to ramble on and on about random things. For her exams, there are a few questions which you MUST hand write (approx 7 - 9 pages). She is definitely a tough grader, and it is hard to get a 1010 on assignments.. The usual score is 810!

She assigns lengthy readings and expects you to participate in class. She wasted a lot of class time lecturing us about how we weren't doing our readings or homework on time. She was unclear on instructions for homework and the final project. Overall, a very frustrating class since she just kept going on about how we weren't working hard enough.
Readings were long, and in class she went off topic when trying to explain them. She wasn't very clear with instructions. Overall, I did terrible in this class even though I should have done better.
Very knowledgable about the topics covered in class. Always willing to help answer questions. Expects you to perform well but is a fair grader. Good at emailing you back.

Doesn't give 1010 and will hardly give out a 9 no matter how good your paper is. Directions are not clear and lectures are usually random and a waste of time. 50 page reading that we didn't even touch on in class.

analysis.name: Hoa Appel
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You know how the best teachers want their students to succeed. This instructor is NOT that. You will get the feeling that she is looking for any random excuse to take away points. She will always comment that you didn't answer the question correctly and mark down for it. She is an extremely unfair grader. You will regret taking her class.

This professor has no regard for students time or well-being. She is a harsh grader, and frequently makes grammatical errors in her coursework. There are zero extra credit opportunities and it is like pulling teeth trying to get an answer regarding any questions for the course. Course content is minimal and useless. AVOID THIS CLASS

Dr. Appel is the best teacher ever. The class was active and fun. Labs were fun to work with. Exams were straightforward;  Dr. Appel takes some questions directly from the lectures, labs, or even in-class activities. She is willing to help her students succeed, she is patient, respects all her students, and is available after class for anyone.

Shes a really nice and approachable professor. All the lecture notes are on canvas for you to look back. Exams are pretty straightforward and not hard as long as youre going through her PowerPoints. Clear grading criteria for your essay, and gives feedback on your draft to show what you need to work on. Do all the assignments, each pt counts.

Prof Appel is nice but a tough grader. A lot of the assignments are busy work and busy reading. I basically took away how to just in-text cite and somewhat APA cite. Class is out of 120 pts so minimal room to make mistakes, only extra credit is up to 5 pts through WACC. Not a hard class, you just need to understand the prompts.

analysis.name: Amy Lambert
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER. DO NOT. lectures go on forever and leave you even more confused. super unclear grading criteria, and then grades VERY harshly. little to no feedback is provided, and when it is, it doesnt make any sense. way too much work for an elective class. spent more time on this than classes for my major. PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF!

Solid professor overall. Sporadic grading. Can grade some assignments instantly and others aren't touched until weeks later. Fun outdoor meet-ups and knowledgeable about ecology. Textbook heavy, so be prepared to write and cite. Can be difficult to reach outside of class, and more strict than other profs when it comes to late work, so be prepared.

I had to drop a class for the first time after taking BIS 319 with Prof. Lambert. Assignments are long, hard to understand, and graded very harshly. She does not have clear expectations on assignments, and does not give good feedback. Almost everyone I talked to in this class was hating it. Do not take!!

This was the first time she taught this course; it was chill. We went outside once a week. There is no hw and there is 1 final exam at the end of the quarter. Each week, a student will present a topic from textbook. If you had to present on the first week, Dr. Lambert will grade you lightly. I skipped the readings and did just fine. STUDY FOR EXAM

Textbook heavy course, but involved and fun. Great if you like hands-on learning. One final exam was easy. All other assignments were participation/completion-based based pretty much. Lots of time outdoors and prof has cool experience in ecology. Can be slow to respond to emails and grade. Wish the timeline was clearer from day 1, though.

analysis.name: Anida Ali

Seems like a tough grader but her gradescale is very easy to exploit as long as you come to class.

She's an artist. She's different, she wants a lot of thought, sharing ideas, people to get out of their comfort zone. She's very lively. Projects have the option of groups or alone. Project require a lot of work. I learned a lot more than expected. A lot about the world. She specializes in installation and performance art.  Good experience.

Stacks a bunch of work for her students in the last two weeks of class and expects her students to finish it all ASAP. It's like she thinks her students only have one class. Replies extremely slow to emails, so don't expect any replies from her for at least two days. Confusing directions when it comes to group projects.

There are 3 professors for this course and Anida is easily the worst one. She'll ask for feedback on a project, but get offended by any comment you make that isn't positive. Her tone is always confrontational, and she will never hesitate to embarrass you in class. She also likes to brag about her odd artwork for 30 minutes every class, so be ready!

awful. If you care at all about your mental health and GPA do not take this professor. She was very rude, and doesn't care about embarrassing you in front of the whole class. She threatens to fail you via email and cc's other classmates, even if you have an A.

analysis.name: Alice Pedersen
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor is awesome. I am taking her again. Her classes are not the easiest, they require a lot of work, but they are conceptually easy to understand, and she does a great job making sure of that. I always felt very comfortable around her and never dreaded class. Everything we learned genuinely felt valuable and relevant. I took BIS 290

BIS 290 Summer '25: She was so chill, kind, gave great feedback, and actually cared about her students. This class was very easy to excel in, as long as you demonstrate your thought process and effort in your writing, you'll get an A. There are a lot of readings assigned, but you only do 3 essays, and the third one is just a revision of 1 of the 2.

(took BIS290) I enjoyed my class with her! She was really kind when I had stuff going on outside of class, and was 100% willing to offer an extension. She wasn't my favorite professor because she felt kind of disingenuous sometimes, but she taught well and was very receptive to feedback, even mid lecture. A no student left behind type of professor.

Such a good class, going into she makes it clear what you got to do to succeed in her class, there's unlimited extra credit opportunities thru WACC, the final is just submitting a final portfolio with all 5 of the papers you work on throughout the quarter, and I really enjoyed the lectures/in-class activities in her class. Recommend 100%

She's great and also the dean of the department. she is very knowledgable. As long as you do assignments and essays on time, easy peasy. she's very easy going, grading based on completion. best writing professor.

analysis.name: Andrew Messamore
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed this class and would recommend him as a professor. You can tell he cares about teaching and creates an environment thats easy to learn and interact in. Attendance counted for 40% of your grade so going to class really matters for his courses. There isn't homework (besides readings) so midterms and attendance define your grade.

I had mixed feelings going into this class, I was not a fan of harry potter or the constant use of AI. However, He had engaging lectures and lots of opportunities for extra credit. There is reading as homework but nothing you submit. 2 midterms and an optional final, he told us what's on the exam and lets you bring 1 page of notes. Overall great.

Very passionate and upbeat about his subject. He split the class into Hogwarts houses and had us compete in four teams through mini-essays with the class as a whole having a Harry Potter theme. No homework, only two written exams. The 2-hour lectures flew by and kept me engaged. The exam prep prompt he makes you do was identical to the exam prompt.

Made class very interesting, 2-hour lecture felt like it went very fast. No homework for SOC 201. Quizzes biweekly. The only part I wish I could change is that the study guide is class-made and prepared two days before the quizzes.

analysis.name: Alexandria Musselman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She's a nice teacher. She makes math alot harder than it is. Participation is graded toughly. She is also a very tough grader marking you down for simple mistakes. Even if you get the answer right you can still be "wrong". I took her up on office hours and still received a low grade. Keep in mind i was a straight A high school student. :( beware

As my first professor, Musselman wasn't a bad teacher. The class felt  like  high school level which was good for people transitioning into college. But her teaching pace was not on the same page as the online textbook which was really bad because tests would always have me confused. If you pay attention and read the online textbook you'll be ok.

Dr. Musselman was an excellent professor for this class! She cares so much about students and is always willing to help you out. As long as you stay on top of all the assignments, which often times she provides ample time to complete during class, you should have a great time. Would definitely take another course with her!

I took her for 124&125, I loved her teaching style. She was very caring, her lectures were super super helpful (definitely attend class), and she wasn't a very tough grader. I think my grade was as good as it was because of how helpful and nice she was.

Professor Musselman encourages students to visit her office hours, which is a plus. HW amount is reasonable, there are two midterms, and a final. She gives the second midterm a week before the final, which is not convenient at all. Teaches the class at a reasonable pace.

analysis.name: Andrea Anthony
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor is almost never available outside office hours in cases of conflicting schedules. Not an understanding professor and is new. Don't take her classes.

Dr. Dre is the best prof ive had for finance! She allows notes on all exams, and her homework and course packets are extremely helpful. As long as u study the hw and packets, you will do just fine. I def had to put in the work/studying, but got a 4.0. She says u have to do the readings, but I did just fine without. TAKE HER!!

She's the best of the best! Her course packets are so useful. You can spend hours reading a textbook and not understand. However, she explains everything in such an easy way, it clicks right away. Definitely do not recommend skipping class as her lectures are amazing. Best finance professor out there. I always look forward to her classes.

Truly cares for your success and will provide you with career help! Extremely organized, uses course packets. For my class it was online so open note/open book which made the midterm and final pretty easy. Homework is also manageable, just do it on time. Lots of additional videos and resources too if needed. Highly recommend Dr. Dre for 350.

Tests aren't relevant to what you learn. Only to some degree. Two group projects aren't too bad, but the tests are horrible:( Doesn't keep things organized, gives you a lot of material to study that overwhelms you. Like I studied around 20 hours a week and still got C+ on the Midterm.

analysis.name: Andrea Stone
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Overall, this class is pretty easy, but the tests can be a little tricky. The exam questions don't always line up directly with what's emphasized in the lectures, so make sure you watch all of her videos. There is one midterm, one final, and a group final. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are in class group assignments for points.

Amazing and very kind professor. She loves to teach and is really helpful if you have questions. She has a really unique interactive assignment, which is actually really fun. If you read and pay attention, tests are easy. Very understanding if you miss class. Overall amazing professor and very sweet.

Professor Stone is by far my favorite professor I've had. She is so helpful and a very good teacher. I took statistics with her and I have never been good at math, but she definitely made it understandable. I really want to take her class again. She can be a bit slow at grading and giving back labs, but if you ask her for it she will give it to you

Class is easy. I only read the first two chapters of the textbook and stopped because the quizzes are based off of her lectures. Every Wednesday, it is lab day; you use and excel program or use equations to fill our the packet/ worksheet. If you don't finish it in class, then it is homework (which isn't due until Monday).

Professor Stone is one of the best teachers that UWB could have!! Not only does she take her time to make sure that the entire class understand the subject, but she does so in a clear and polite manner. If you need to take BIS312, take it from her, NOT FROM CARLISLE.

analysis.name: Dundon Ariana

review_highlights.comment: Drops lowest exam, lecture HW not accepted late (5%), 48-hour grace period w/o penalty + lowest 2 scores dropped for HW (15%), participation of 10 pts for on-time arrival and staying for whole class period (5%), weekly quizzes w/option to work in pairs (15%), in-class work have 24-hour grace period w/o penalty (5%) Exams- 17.5% each, Final - 20%

The midterms in this class will make or break you. I ended up having to drop the class for that exact reason. She's an extremely tough grader on tests. If you're bad at exams like I am, I honestly wouldn't recommend taking this class. Very kind professor, but one test will really determine if you'll pass the class or not.

Her classes are great to learn in, super engaging, and really go through the process, giving time. Though her grading is super tough, it is super test heavy, one okay or bad midterm will absolutely be detrimental to your grade.

Very test and quiz heavy, although good professor overall. She always helps with any questions during classes. Your grade is very dependent on how much effort you put into the class, as well as showing up and scoring well on ALL the quizzes and midterms (and final).

Assigns lots of homework every day, multiple assignments a day. Does not lecture in class whatsoever, you have to watch about an hour of lecture before every class on your own. Quizzes every week, and does not give any partial credit on exams.

analysis.name: Arnie Lund
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lund is okay. I thought his lectures were quite difficult to pay attention to, and that I could easily go over the same material on my own. Lots of group projects which he grades fairly, but the tests are what can tank your grade. He asked some specific questions about something a guest speaker said that is almost impossible to remember.

This class was very disorganized. He tends to ramble about his industry experience and his lectures were very irrelevant and borderline confusing due to the information overload. That being said, you get a double-sided note sheet for all exams, and he is a very easy grader. Overall, not a good teacher, but good for industry knowledge and easy A.

Fantastic teacher. He is an experienced industry veteran. Very lecture heavy, however, you are allowed a cheat sheet for exams which is all you will need. Show up, pay attention in class, and take occasional notes, and you will 100% do well. Invites guest speakers to class to speak on the industry and group projects are very fun and educational.

Arnie's classes are easy as long as you do the assigned work. There are a lot of small assignments, but you typically get full credit on them. You're in a group the entire quarter to complete a lot of these assignments. Tests are pretty easy, you get a cheat sheet and he curves tests down so you can often get over 100%

analysis.name: Arnie Berger

Another thing, half our class failed the midterm and most got a C, in summary he said "do better". Def get the book and study ALOT

Dr. Berger is a very knowledgeable professor who loves what he does. However, he does not know how to teach students. He doesn't really go through problems with the students and kind of just leaves it up to the students to do it themselves.
The worst class and professor is in my scholar live. He will give you the most challenge problem, and his lecture is not helpful. At the end of the quarter, he will curve your grade. Painful memory!

Berger is clearly a knowledgeable professor, this does not transfer that well to his lecture abilities. If you are reliant on lectures to learn, please practice using textbook questions. I didn't feel that the lectures helped.

He's just terrible. He only read off the PowerPoint. Worksheets are not relevant to the exam or quizzes. I tried every method in the book to study for this class, but no matter how much I studied, the quizzes and exams were still unpredictable. Try to take this class with another professor, if not GOOD LUCK!

analysis.name: Aseem Datar

review_highlights.comment:
In tune with modern times and refreshing to see a real world approach. Bonus - does an interview workshop and helped me prep for a real job interview that I cleared! 

Really cares and spent even a weekend helping us think on our project. Highly highly recommend.
wonderful class, cares about students. Even does an interview workshop to connect to real world....
Fun yet engaging class. I wish he taugh more often..

If this class has an opening run towards it. Amazing lectures and to the point. Aseem is a great presenter and makes things simple to digest. My only suggestion would be to make this two hours.

Very clear lectures, easy to understand. Not many assignments and only 1 exam and 1 group project. Attendance is very important because class discussions are a big part of your grade. This guy seriously sucks. He blazed through 2/3 of the material in the first four weeks and spent the rest of the quarter letting us go through "practice problems". Terrible lecturer. Do you like stupid Dilbert comic strips? Then you'll love all of Berger's class material. If you can stand his dry humor and snide personality, you'll make it through

Had a different experience with Berger in EE.  He definitely knows his field of EE, but was disinterested in teaching any classes other than 422.  Repeats the same stories which wastes time. If you really can delay this class hoping that litterly any other professors teach it, please do so. analysis.name: Aseef Nilkund
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

Aseef is the reason I got to computer science. He is passionate, caring, and motivational. I would recommend taking him. It is always funny that I kept stuck on setters and getters which is a simple concepts but he has pushed me through it until I became really good in programming.

Amazing at articulating programming concepts. I knew nothing about programming before his class, and he helped me understand everything. he don't really teach. he sits on the corner and students present the entire quarter except for few hrs. not well prepared for classes, assignment is not clear, grading criteria is not clear. not recommended if you care to know the material well

analysis.name: Hazel Asuncion
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you like hands on, group projects, and active participation this class is great. Her lecture notes are great and most of the tests will be taken straight from her lecture notes. The class will be easy if you have a good group. There are 5 group projects that really require a lot of group interaction.

Professor is very unorganized, creating confusion for students. Students never know where assignments are, always having to email the professor to ask. She always responds by saying she messed up or forgot.  Boring lectures as she reads off of slides and randomly calls on students. This is not high school, relax with the cold calls.

Hazel gets the job done. She doesn't have exceptional lectures, but cares about you learning the material. Her system for group projects was solid, since you can 'escape' from bad groups after each project if needed. Overall, she will help you learn if you put in effort. Ask questions, get assistance and above all, participate.

If this class's content was relevant to current trends in the tech industry, like user research, defining tech stacks, and different problem-solving frameworks, it would be one of the best classes in the CSS program. Hazel is a great professor and great resource for future knowledge, but her lessons are outdated.

This class seemed like such a waste of money. All class is essentially answering questions from your reading. There is no engagement so you just lose all of the knowledge the next week. Keeping engaged is also extremely difficult. The contents of the class are fairly easy however. Do yourself a favor and take this in person with a different prof.

analysis.name: Athirai Irissappane
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: TCSS422 is an operating system class. Overall, the class content was pretty hard itself. She just made it worse. I studied very hard for the midterm because I messed up some of her random quizzes during class and did pretty good on it. However, she somehow canceled the third HW and made quizzes worth 10%(was about 6%). I lost 5% for no reason.

I wouldn't take her class she has no idea what she is doing and her lectures are very scattered. Also she updates homework assignments a day before they are due because she made a mistake making the assignment impossible. She is also very rude to talk with.
She's really a nice professor. I studied Machine Learning under TCSS555. Extra credits are useful to boost your grade. Emphasis very much on feedback. The difficulty is not so much.
The professor has a clear grading criteria and she is vocal about it. She's strict and expects students to follow the criteria set by professors for evaluation.

Lowkey never showed up but she always put effort into me succeeding. Fun group projects, quite a few readings, and a lot of just talking even if it wasn't about the subject in class. If you can take her, DO IT

Very Supportive. She will give you a lot of resources throughout the quarter.
The class is interesting as well. You will learn about how climate change was discovered in the first place.
Her grading is very reasonable and kind. Reasonable homework amount.
By far the best BCORE class to take as your very first class in college.

analysis.name: Wayne Au

review_highlights.comment: I thought he was average. He definitely has the male ego thing going on.

This was a very easy class and I actually enjoyed it more than I thought I would!! Super nice prof although we were online, he made sure to provide help to students. I wish he was more responsive outside of class though. If you see prof Wayne Au listed for a class, sign up! :)

I'm taking him for BEDUC 201: special topics in diversity and education, topic "asian Americans in education," and the class is based on the book he published. Assignments are pretty much just reading and leaving annotations on the reading and then interpreting each chapter in a 250-500 word response. Didn't interact with the instructor much, but I'd say I learned a decent amount about Asian American education.
The class was easy and so was the workload. Overall, the class was chill and allowed me to learn about the topic without having to stress and worry as much. It made doing the assignments more fun.

analysis.name: Murat Ayhan

I had no clue what my grade was the whole quarter. He is pretty tough tough grader but I wouldn't recommend taking him honestly.

I mean if you want to learn go for it. But if you care about your grade PLEASE CHOOSE ANOTHER PROFESSOR. His grading system is chaotic and he expects you to print everything. I see people saying he is funny...he isn't.

analysis.name: Ryan Burns

Ask for extra credit assignments. I had to fight for points
Prof is inaccessible and clearly is forced to teach this class. He is clearly overwhelmed and checked out.

analysis.name: Patricia Bravo
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

Did not make any announcements about the first day of school being asynchronous. Group projects are crucial and assigned, so you gotta hope you get a GOOD group.

This professor will intentionally choose to over complicate the class because she herself does not feel that what she teaches is important. And she is absolutely right. The last 10 weeks we have discussed the exact same thing over and over again. She is also a bit biased, I've noticed colored students get penalized more than non colored ones.

analysis.name: Casey Mann

That being said, the class is HARD and there is SO much homework. Tied for the most homework I've had.

80% of your grade is exams and unless you're an above average student you're going to struggle and probably fail this class. His HW takes an absurd amount of time to complete. His class average GPA for the quarter was 1.8 and the average score for his final exam was 57%. He fails his students just as much as his students fail his class. Avoid him.

She's honestly a great teacher. You learn so much and its simple. Her vibe is great, she is very likeable.

analysis.name: Tasha Buttler

By far one of the best teachers I've ever had and I doubt ill ever meet a teacher as great as her.She's definitely not an easy teacher nor, an easy grader, but if u stay focused and need her help, she's more then gladly to do whatever it takes to help so you can learn the material and get the grade you deserve.Ican honestly say I loved her class!

Professor Buttler is an incredible teacher. She is very intelligent and is truly invested in the success of students who want to succeed and improve in their writing. analysis.name: Caleb Trujillo

He made the class very interesting at times through various activities, some that will make you step out of your comfort zone. The required book is extremely boring. The bad thing about his course was that his assignments were often very confusing, not according to just me but other students as well. Required a Community Based Learning (volunteer).

I do not understand the positive feedback for this prof. I took a class with him last quarter and it was a mistake.  No feedback on work over the entire course of the quarter. Then he missed the end of quarter grade deadline by over a week. I got blindsided with the lowest grade of my school career! 2 full grades lower than chem and bio.  Avoid!!

analysis.name: Steven Collins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The most worthless class I have ever taken at UWB.  This class was a waste of time and only added stress to my schedule.  The professor is willing to give extra help, but his explainations are not well thought out.  There are numerous times in class where he confuses himself with the problems he assigns.  If you don't need BIS 250, don't take it.

If you need Motion and Mechanics BIS 250, take Steve. A great intro to basic physics, and he's one of the most laid back, knowledgeable, and good-humored profs I've had. It's not all nuts and bolts, and Steve makes the course interesting by including the scientists and their place in history. Fascinating, fun course. Flexible final exam, to boot.

His exam prep materials are great, but lectures aren't the greatest. He confuses himself a lot and  freezes mid-lecture to stare at his notes. It's not his fault though. He never taught fluid mechanics before, and I think he was forced to. Exams are easy, and he always posts solutions for practice problems ,so studying is pretty painless for me.

I loved him. He has a solid voice that you can hear anywhere in the room and he is very excited about the material he teaches. The thermo series is  difficult, so prepare to read a lot & do TONS of practice problems. But, quizzes are straight from the HW so that's good. And 40% of the final was take home! Very approachable & willing to help u.

He is a very self-less professor, always giving to his students. The dude brings in coffee and croissants to my 8:45 to help wake students. Summarizes tough material in packets and is very clear cut with grading and expectations. He struggles a bit with material, but fluid dynamics was never easy and he hasn't ever taught it. Good stuff.

analysis.name: Stevi Costa
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: In her Zoom class right now. Love her. She may seem eccentric and is a little disorganized, but she is so dedicated to keeping a positive environment in class and it shows. You'll have to write a lot but the books are great. She also encourages students to talk with her outside class about their interests - which I did because we share interests.

FANTASTIC class. Please please please take anything you can with her - she is so kind, caring, and understanding. I go to office hours all the time just cause I feel comfortable talking with her about the class and our shared interests. Don't listen to the person below. If you ever read this, love you Stevi! (from JL - also why do I have 115%)

I cannot say enough good things about her. I am in the same class as the person below and I agree - she's definitely eccentric, but is so engaging and caring that it's not an issue. She's very open about her personal life, and wants students to get to know her outside of the lecture setting - something not enough people take advantage of. Love her.

Stevi is great and passionate about literature. BIS387 is basically a book club and it's super fun if you like reading. I genuinely enjoyed the novels. We read 4 and there was only 1 that I disliked. The reading quizzes are easy if you keep up with the novel. She only grades on reading quizzes and the final. Discussions are complete/not complete.

We missed a lot of days of class. I think she's nice and a good prof to take in person but she doesn't seem to understand that there's a difference between online and on campus. It's not uncommon for a single week to have 100 pages of reading along with a quiz and a mandatory "discussion." She grades easily and responds quickly to emails.

analysis.name: Colin Danby
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: While he had a lot of negative feedback for my work, along with everyone else in the class, I managed to pull an A. I did the work, used his feedback and attended office hours. HOWEVER: He's not very nice,it's difficult to understand what he wants from you, the work is not really relevant (other than brushing up writing skills) and so boring.

Do not take. The homework was manageable, but his grading is insanely unfair. He will write comments at the bottom that doesn't make sense, even if you clearly answer his questions. getting a 0 or below half credit after actually being right about something because you didn't perfectly mimic his description of it is the worst part.

Avoid

The class I took with him, is a hybrid class. We learn on our own and see him in person once a week. I almost failed my first exam because my definition wasn't exactly word to word in the textbook. He's a very harsh grader and nitpicking over the smallest thing. The exams are hard if you don't teach yourself but the homework is really easy.

He's an insanely strict grader. Every other writing class or writing related class I've gotten good grades, he picks on random things and completely fails you. He does not care if you have family emergencies or anything. I highly recommend not taking any of his classes unless you want to put all your effort in and get a terrible grade.

BBUS220/BIS200 It's surprising how many bad reviews Danby has. He's really nice and seems super passionate. He give us one homework a week and our midterm was literally identical to the practice he gave us. Danby does his best to make it as easy as possible. If you just show up to class and follow along you don't actually need to study at all.

analysis.name: Shannon Cram
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is one of the funnest classes I've ever taken. Shannon is very friendly and helpful. She even went out of her way to give me extra feedback upon request. Her curriculum is not boring and provides a great opportunity for critical thinking. She adapted to students with learning and social disabilities, which I've seen other profs struggle with.

Never a dull lecture with professor Cram! She is very passionate about technological ethics and extremely approachable both in and out of class. 

The class itself has a very manageable workload and no finals or midterms, points mostly come from participation and weekly responses then a final group project. 10/10 would recommend to anyone!

Attendance is graded like it's high school or something, students really should have the freedom to come to class for more support and information, or read and complete work outside of class on one's own time if they wish. On the bright side, Cram is at least seemingly lenient with grading so far...

Great professor! She is new here but she is an exceptional teacher. She is extremely helpful and makes the class assignments fun. She is also very inspirational and has a really cool story, she is a cancer survivor and works cleanup at Hanford Nuclear site. Everyone in the class definitely really liked and respected her. She definitely listens too.

If you ever have a chance to take a class with Shannon Cram, do it. She is a phenomenal teacher, caring and passionate person that wants everyone to learn and have fun doing it. The class structure flowed so well that it left you wanting more! Her energy carries when she lectures keep you engaged and intrigued. She makes classes you want to go to

analysis.name: Johanna Crane
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Readings are interesting & important for class discussions. Every class we have a discussion & group project on that reading. We get to only do 6 250 worded reading responses out of 11.  Some days class consists of videos which was cool. She's easy-going, a chill prof. No tolerance on phones& laptop use (unless for readings).

First quarter at UW Bothell. Really enjoyed her class and I thought overall she was a great teacher. BIS300 was pretty damn easy too! Would definitely recommend her. Just make sure you are willing to participate in groupclass discussions. Attendence was said to be mandatory at the beginning but after the first few weeks she stopped taking it.

She's a good teacher with a very strong passion for teaching. She's clear, informative, and nice. Assigns quite a bit of reading and the class, unfortunately, was rather boring. Lots of essays, but as long as you follow her prompts and read the readings, you'll be fine. Does require a group project and presentation.

Draws class material from many different publications, most of which she scans into a pdf so you can print them off for free. Not the best at explaining her expectations for assignments and projects, but not horrible. Assigns a lot of groupwork. Probably won't take her again if I can help it.

I really enjoyed this professor.  It was a tough class, but she was clear in what she wanted and she set up the class so that we had to do a little at at time towards a big project.  If I had more time at school, I would have tried to take more classes with her.

analysis.name: Sharon Crowley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
