review_highlights.comment: Sharon is very nice. We had a lot of readings to do for homework and we wrote a lot of short papers, but at the end for your final grade she will give you a grade based on how much your short papers improved upon the course of the quarter.

1. We do very little actual writing during class, she treats class like a lecture 2. She sometimes goes into the TMI area. I don’t want to know my teacher has ADD, that’s personal information I don’t want to know about 3. Its a very disengaging class: she talks through most of it. Not structured. 4. Posts grades leisurely Take at your own risk

One of my favorite teachers I have ever had. Extremely helpful, extremely fun, and keeps things interesting. She is really kind and cares a lot about her students. I've taken 3 classes with her and all have been fairly difficult but I really enjoyed them thanks to her.

She grades extremely hard. Very hard to get a good grade in her class. She does not posts grades on time. She is a very boring instructor although she "tries" to make it fun but its not. You should avoid just plainly for the sake of your grades.
She is a nice teacher. In her class, she does a lot of fun stuff. However, it is difficult to get a good grade in her class. She is strict when grading your work.

analysis.name: Caren Crandell
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This was her first time teaching BIS301 so I tried to be forgiving, but ... She often didn't post assignment materials until 3am  the morning it was due, waited until finals week to give feedback on research paper drafts, had everyone research GRASS! Because of in class work, you need to go to do well, but it's a waste of time. Nice lady, but jeez.

Second week of classes and she's already having us have a midterm on one lecture which is just plain terminology. This wouldn't be bad if it wasn't at least 50 slides (at most 75) with at least 2 terms on each slide. We also never went over this in lecture and never talked about it again. Definitely would not take if not required.

Very disorganized, long-winded directions. The coursework wasn't that bad, but every little assignment had pages of time-wasting contradicting directions and dates for no reason. Did weird things like "study guides are optional unless you want an A." They were points worth 10% of your grade. Everything is optional if you don't want the points....

I have never gotten less than a 3.5 in a class and I am pretty sure i am about to fail hers. I have done all of the readings, studied each power point, and have stayed up late preparing for each quiz. I feel like I have learned a lot of information but if you look at my quiz scores, you would never know this. Her tests do not reflect your effort.

Long unorganized lectures . Canvas site is also unorganized. Opens drop boxes hours before assignments are due. Takes months to grade work. Not very responsive by email. But... she is very passionate about ecology. My recommendation: only take this class if it's in your major, you really enjoy ecology, and aforementioned points won't bother you.

analysis.name: Nick Cuhaciyan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This project management course focuses on real experience you can actually use, not just theory. We worked through real scenarios, learned professional communication, and got helpful feedback. I left with skills I've already used in interviews and team projects. Truly prepares you for the workplace!

Just finished my last class of the quarter with this guy. He went out of his way to spend time with each team to review processes that are applicable in the real world. He gave extra credit when needed and even spent his own money to buy the class food to celebrate our project. Never had a class like this before, awesome.

They explain things in a way that actually makes sense, and throw in examples that make class less boring. Workload can be a bit much sometimes but it's not busywork, it actually helps you get the material. They're easy to talk to and pretty helpful if you're stuck. Overall a solid prof if you don't mind group work.

Do not work with stuck-up petty and difficult people from day 1! Please switch to a group that has less people and work with them or you will suffer with revenge grading on peer evals that is worth most of your grade second half of the quarter. RUN, this destroyed my GPA.
Refreshing change of pace from the grind of glass. Grading is set up so those who don't show up can't get a free ride. Professor seems reasonable to handle class issues when they come up.

analysis.name: Cynthia  Karlsson

review_highlights.comment: This is for 437 only. Her class is an absolute nightmare. She does not teach in class and expects a lot out of her challenge assignments. HOW do you expect us to learn how to calculate budgets, FTE's, and be specific in our variables when you don't teach what that looks like????????????

She is not tech savvy, which leads to complications when using Canva. The assignments do not feel connected to the final project, making the course seem disorganized. The class feels sporadic and lacks cohesion. Class time is not used effectively, and she struggles to engage the entire class. Much of the time in this course feels unproductive.

She can be really unorganized and she gets very frazzled easily which made me lose confidence in her. She made us take a quiz on a concept she gave the wrong formula for, saw the class failed, and had us retake it. Day of the retake she struggled to teach us the correct steps for an hour and then let us struggle on our own. She's very nice though.

Worksheets for weeks 1-7 (5 pts), discussion posts + response for weeks 1-10 (5 pts) + lowest score dropped, in-class work (10 pts) + lowest score dropped, midterm + final exams (15 pts each), Health issue brief final (25 pts), assignments submitted over 1 week late lose 25% for each week, due dates and assignment instructions unclear frequently

manage large class bad. kind professor. organization unclear. leaving the rest of class with no guidance

objectives each week not explained. assigned readings not reviewed. expected to apply concepts in assignments. connection for in-class activities and course is not clear

examples overly simple not aligned with course level

review_highlights.comment:
Cynthia Chang was amazing!! I took her and Jennifer Atkinson's combined bcore 110 class fall 2024 and it was a good decision. Be ready to participate and meet new people bc the whole class is based on groupwork. If you're looking for a fun bcore with reasonable workload, then it's perfect :) 
(Also the textbook is free if I remember correctly)

This is an easy A class if you understand the material you don't need to go to in depth into the material as she lets you use pervious tests that she uploads to canvas on the exam as notes (laptop notes are fine) but you can't look up answers. She is very nice. Lectures are boring tho. 3 tests and 1 final the lowest test gets dropped finals don't.

She's very sweet and passionate about the topic, making it more engaging. However, as others have said, she writes on her lecture slides as she goes along and they do not save, so if you want to keep track of that, you may want to ensure you show up. Exams are open-note and if you study previous exams and the answer keys, you'll likely do well!

I actually took her for BCORE 104 
-class takes place both ON and OFF campus 
-need a car to access if not you need a carpool
-Lots of pointless readings
-very passionate about subject but not great at grading
-Easy to pass
-Docs points from group projects without good reasons
-No tests or quizzes
-Mostly busy work/ readings
-nice professor

SO easy to understand, she gives the best lectures i have ever received. If you take notes and review her material she gives to study YOU WILL PASS and even get a good grade. Really easy to fall behind but she really cares about her students.

analysis.name: Dariush Khaleghi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DK was the best prof. I've ever had. He is a very funny guy, but can seem intimidating at first. He is very passionate and has lots of debates during his lectures. Attendance does matter. Very easy grader and cares more about effort than anything else. No midterm, optional final, one quarter-long group project.

I had DK this fall quarter and he was great! Super funny (I often couldn't stop laughing in class), understanding, and has very clear instructions. 

By far one of the best professors at UWB. The material is connected to real world issues that matter and he does a great job expressing higher level concepts in a simple manner. 

Highly recommend

I felt this professor made several inappropriate comments that felt sexist or hurtful to students. This discouraged students from engaging in the class. He verbatim said, "I hate my wife" which was incredibly inappropriate. The class structure was disorganized and instructions were not clear. If the professor likes you, you will get a good grade.

Openly speaks about hating woman like his wife, made fun of a woman in my class because she had tattoo's. he started every single class saying he was a " dictator " just like Donald Trump and Elon musk....I have never felt compelled to write such a review.

He was rude to students during class. At time we made discriminatory comments (I don't think he was ill-intended, but still). Huge ego and picked on students; he made us purchase the McGraw hill online book ($150+) and very heavy on group projects. He was not a really tough grader tho, if he liked you, you didn't have any issues

analysis.name: Joseph Decuir
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I've taken multiple EE labs with Joe and appreciate his wisdom and experience. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. As long as you show up, participate, are respectful, and put the effort in, then you will pass. Don't arrive late and don't talk while he is explaining the labs as it's rude and you'll get on his bad side.

He's nice but his grading makes no sense. he'll dock points for things not mentioned in the lab manual in a vague sentence. Pretty much every link posted doesn't work. Asking him for help/a question usually leads to a semi-related answer then to an unrelated topic and trying to get the answer you want feels re-prompting an ai over and over
Joe is a super chill dude I've heard he yaps but he has a lot of knowledge and cares about the students

Be prepared to cover the same 3 same presentations slides over 3 months. Talks about himself constantly. Examples are given from the perspective of his own experience and it is always the same story! Interrupts Professor Hannachi constantly. Not sure if they are supposed to be a team or if Joe is trying to establish dominance.

analysis.name: Marie Deschene
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took CSS315 with her, and it was frustrating. She and her TA nitpicked minor details, leading to unfair point deductions. Attendance was strict—even if you were sick and couldn't join online, you'd still lose 10 points. Feedback was vague, and her rigid “my way or the highway” approach made learning difficult. I wouldn't recommend her class.

This teacher gives very little feedback if at all, and grading is based on "improvement" rather than actual measurable metrics. You need a 100% or above to get a 4.0, but extra credit is not given and if you miss points on even one assignment that drops you down to at most a 3.9. Office hours are both useless and the only way you will pass.

Marie is a nice person but not a good professor. The layout of this class is awful and doesn't make sense (e.g. we learned grammar at the end of the quarter). Terrible feedback and very subjective grading. If a quiz answer is not word for word then expect a 0 on that question. It's impossible to receive a 4.0 if you don't get 100% on everything.

Not the best class I've taken at UWB. This isn't the professors fault but the cybersecurity curriculum is a hot mess and pretty disorganized. Lectures for about an hour each class, and you are given a very long worksheet afterwards. Class is sort of interesting but mostly boring. A good grade is doable in this class but a 4.0 is impossible.

301 has serious academic problems. there is no thinking allowed and you will be graded down based on the metadata in your word document. Marie is not helpful and admits to grading based on opinion. office hours are a joke. she makes incorrect quiz questions multiple times and wont admit it, grades harshly and isn't flexible. take Sinclair.

analysis.name: Patrick Detroit
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Patrick is probably one of my favorite professors at UWB. He is so incredibly awesome, and takes time to get to know his students. He is lecture heavy, but he posts all of his notes online and they really help! I would totally recommend taking him at least once if you have the chance.
Perkins teaching style is amazing. Even through the class can feel tough at times, I always felt like I could ask him for help or a better explanation.
Great lecturer, often had short class sessions depending on topic. Extremely supportive of students. Office hours were by appointment but he was very helpful and often available after class.

Patrick was an amazing lecturer! Although I don't understand anything in manufacturing, his operations class was manageable with the help of littlefield simulation, stratapult experiments and boeing tour. A lot of team work is required for classes and he doesn't give any instructions for projects, but he is very laid back. Cares about his students!

I've been in college 6 years; majored in engineering, culinary arts, and accounting between 4 different colleges , and Patrick Detroit was the best teacher I've ever had. I don't care who else is teaching this class. Go out of your way to take this professor. You'll learn, you'll have a tremendous amount of fun, and you won't even work that hard.

analysis.name: Kim Cunningham
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Kim Cunningham is sweet and caring, but I wouldn't recommend her if you want to learn. Lectures are fast-paced, lacking substance as she reads off the slides. Answers to questions and instructions can be vague and unclear, which made both projects a bit more stressful than they should be. Assignments do not help on exams or quizzes.

I took her class for 210 last quarter and had to take her again for 211 because I didn't have much of a choice. For both quarters, she constantly cancels class (we had to present our group project on zoom in 210 because she canceled class).  Lectures are very long and boring I just go over the slides. Assignments are long too.

Didn't see her in person once this quarter and that was fine with me, but I can see it being frustrating for others. Learned more from the "Connect" textbook that she uses but she was very sweet and not a harsh grader. She only manually grades projects (2 total), and her feedback was good. Multiple assignments due onone day at the end of each unit.

This class was very easy to pass but i felt like i didn't truly learn anything. I signed up for a hybrid class but something came up literally every day we had an in-person class scheduled and the entire quarter ended up being remote. She seems nice but just reads off of slides we're given. She is very good at responding to emails fast though
Honestly if you are going to take professor Kim's "In person" classes don't even bother buying parking passes. She has canceled EVERY class this quarter.

analysis.name: Raissa DeSmet

review_highlights.comment: she was great, great energy, great topics and I loved coming to class. she was also very helpful on assignments or if you needed accommodations. the only thing I didn't like was how assignments were posted with very short notice and not at the start of the week.

I wouldnt say Professor DeSmet was horrible, but she wasnt great either. I took this class because of the great ratings and I regret my decision. Throughout the entire quarter there were maybe 6-7 assignments and she doesnt grade them until the very end of the quarter. You literally have no idea how your doing. Please take anyone else

Raissa is one of the most amazing professors I have had. I took her course last winter and she was so helpful, so clear with her instructions, and she gave a lot of feedback on the final. She allows you to express who you are in class as well!

I like that professor desmet doesnt lecture the entire class and gives us breaks. She is decent, she definitely isnt a 5/5 easy 4.0 professor. It has been 6 ish weeks in the quarter and she hasnt graded anything. Dont take her.

analysis.name: Denis Trapido
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dennis is there to help you pass and succeed. This is pretty much an easy class and as long as you try then you will be fine. There is a lot of group work involved, group papers and assignments so be prepared to collaborate.

The book that he uses is a good source. However, his grading method is kind of weird. Pop quizzes is 30% of your grade, so come to class and make sure you can take all the quizzes. There are just 4 pop quizzes but drop one. The questions are just about have you read the reading, not necessary apply to what you learn from reading.

Professor Trapido is one of the impactful professors I have ever had. His class simulations are fun and are very applicable to the real world. He really cares whether the students are getting something from the lessons he makes. His lessons have helped me mature from a personal sense and a professional sense. 10/10 would take this professor again.

I had the privilege of being a student of Professor Trapido's "Management of Organizations" course in my first quarter at UW Bothell.  Professor Trapido is one of my favorite professors at the UW Bothell School of Business.  Not only was his course fun and enlightening, but he is very personable and caring.  I absolutely recommend his course(s).

A really awesome prof who cares a lot about the learning of his students. We played a lot of games and simulations that relate to the coursework that were both fun and a great learning experience. Read BEFORE class to be prepared for discussions + pop quizzes (which are mostly easy comprehension). Stay on track + do reading and it won't be hard

analysis.name: Diana Garcia-Snyder

review_highlights.comment: To provide some insight on when I took this professor. I took her in spring quarter of 2018. She is my dance teacher, very nice.

really caring and respectful. one of the nicest teachers I know

analysis.name: Michael Dimeo

Great guy, don't arrive late to class, he'll flip . . .otherwise a great teacher/professor.  you'll learn-from and enjoy his class . . it's a guarantee.

A sweet professor. Course will be difficult to understand if you're not good at science like me but with dedication you can understand well. She's very kind & sweet, it helps lower any class anxiety. Good at teaching, she makes panapto recordings too.

One of the BEST professors of all time, her classes are engaging, workload is very fair, passionate about her classes and is always willing to help out. I was not confident with this topic, but this professor made me genuinely excited to learn, and she provides extra help with study guides that ACTUALLY help you with the tests.

analysis.name: Dong Si

I have to say I learned a lot from this course and his is really a nice guy. I like  the bonus question part of discussion and term project and the way he make complicated concept easy to understand .   could have more written homework  instead of just programming.

Always easy to talk to and ready to help, the professor created a positive and welcoming classroom atmosphere that really supported our learning. Professor Si's course structure, slides, and explaining every topic by helping us come up with examples ourselves and think of solutions to problems was great. The group discussion we had in
class were also very helpful because I got to know different perspectives of the concepts.

analysis.name: Maurice Dolberry

review_highlights.comment: Creates assignments out of seemingly no where, doesn't post things ahead of time, nor will he post assignments even after he's assigned them. I took his class after reading the ratings on here and was scared but it was the best class i ever took and he is the best teacher i ever had. As a person of color especially. analysis.name: Andrew Jorgenson

Pay attention in lecture, do the homework yourself, you don't need the text book, ask questions if you're stuck, and engage in his lectures.

Attendance is not mandatory unless for exams. Homework is easy if you pay attention in lectures. Almost impossible to reach out to him outside of class or office hours. Not a very good professor. Videos in class and a group project to end it all.

This professor made writing very easy. She broke down the process and walked us through it with weekly lectures. She responds quickly to emails and is willing to accommodate students who have trouble. She gives great feedback! Would def take her again.

Absolutely love Shari. She is super flexible with deadlines and provides amazing feedback. Lots of homework but it's totally doable. She is also very quick to respond if you need any help and she truly cares about what she teaches.

review_highlights.comment: If you're a health studies major, you can't avoid her but this is a warning for you. This prof is one of those who is more interested in showing off in front of the students than help them learn. He knows a finite set of things and anything other than that would just be a waste of time asking him. Doesn't teach a single thing in class but the assign&exams are so confusing and useless that everyone scores less and feel demotivated.

Kelvin is the worst professor I've had at UW. Unavailability, a concerning lack of flexibility, respect, and consideration, paired with a goofy accent and a demeaning manner is the tip of the iceberg. Never take this prof's lessons, he always gives lots of tasks and homework... and unnecessary to take this course, it is not helpful for your future work literally...

analysis.name: Camas Key
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: One of the nicest/most personable profs Ive had at UW across both campuses! He really does his best to present the material in the most easy to understand way, so if youre struggling with something, let him know. Assigned textbook was also helpful. Very reasonable grading and tests are fair & reflective of things from lecture, worksheets, hw etc.

Awesome teacher who actually cares about his students success. He is a very positive and upbeat guy, which makes the class fun. Half the class is lecturing, second half is working on worksheets in groups. His tests are not bad either as long as you pay attention in class. He allows for a page of notes front and back. Would recommend 10/10!

Dr. Key is a great professor. I like his way of lecturing - half group work, half lecture. He has a happy personality, and is eager to help. Seems like he actually wants to be there teaching you! His tests, so far, are easy - part t/f, part multiple choice, and some short answer. The homework really helps you understand the concepts. And he's cute!

The best physics professor at UWB hands down! He cares about his students success. It takes a minute to get used to how he teaches, but eventually the class flows well. Tests are pretty easy. Would highly recommend.

Everything I've ever wanted in a professor. He's just incredible. Physics is weird, because you have to see the world through a new lensthat's where my struggle was. If you want to actually learn "physics," I couldn't recommend another professor more highly than Dr. Key. He made class engaging and fun, good luck finding that from someone else. ��

analysis.name: Deanna Kennedy

review_highlights.comment: Interesting and entertaining class. Course layout was very organized and clear. A wide variety of sims and activities to bring topics into real-world applications. Wasn't a horrible teacher but wouldn't take again. She often would get confused when lecturing and look back at her notes or correct what she had said. Also didn't explain cases and projects in depth. Really nice lady though and although I struggled ended up w 3.4. Suggestion prof: split the projects between the quarter instead of both at the end!

The load for this class was more then I have ever had for any other 5 credit class. We were assigned tons of problems (from Pearson) which did little to nothing to improve what I really know about the subject on top of several group projects and 2 field trips (Who goes on field trips in college?).

She uses Pearson Labs for her homework which automatically detracts from the class. I honestly didn't learn anything in this class. The homework was pointless and took FOREVER. She doesn't even include the homework on the tests. The tests are based on in-class lectures so you can't miss class.

She gives you example tests  but the real tests are Way more difficult. She doesn't always do or not do what she says.  Homework is extensive. Projects instructions not clear  and grading criteria changes midstream. She has great experience but isn't able to communicate her knowledge.

analysis.name: Kevin Kim
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kim is an extremely engaging and thoughtful professor. He knows his material very well. Dr. Kim is very reasonable when it comes to grading. Very discussion oriented. He is not so much concerned with what you say, but how you substantiate your claim. Overall, I highly recommend him!

Professor Kim gave good, informational lectures and assigned interesting reading material. Expectations on assignments were clear, and I appreciated the feedback he gave when grading papers and tests.

What impressed me most about Prof  Kim was his desire for input.  He consistently gauged how we felt about the content, if we needed more time in our groups, etc.. You can tell he wants to ensure people want to be there and feel they are getting what they need out of it. He is also extremely knowledgable so you will learn plenty. Recommend for sure

The majority of what I took away from this class came from in-class discussions. These consisted of Prof. Kim inviting us to build our own individual views of the issues of the periods/concepts we were studying.  He absolutely wants you to succeed. He's open to having email/in-person conversations to make sure that everyone understands what to do.

Dr. Kim approaches American Capitalism from multiple perspectives to encompass more than the traditional historical approach you learn in high school and contemporary news. He allows for you to understand trends and changes in different locations that helped create the form of Capitalism we experience today. Great objective Prof.

She is very nice and pretty!If you attend the class regularly, then you will be ok!

I took this class after hearing some good things about the teacher and it's been the easiest class I've taken so far. While there are a few essays you need to write, there's a lot of freedom in your topics so as long as you do something you enjoy, it shouldn't be bad.
I took her art and healthcare class and i loved her! Very nice and understanding,, we had snow days and she told us to not even worry about coming! Learned a lot in this class too!
She is sort of disorganized, but she is so nice and sweet. She is willing to get to know the students and very friendly. She is also an easy grader.

review_highlights.comment: Lakshmana is a really kind hard working professor who uses his depth of knowledge to provide in detail explanations and his humor makes the lectures lots of fun while being mostly well focused. He has a great balance between encouragement and challenge, always pushing students to do their best. Although the course was not the easiest for me, his support and humor made it a great experience.

Super friendly, his humor made lectures fun! Homework is pretty heavy but it's a hard subject in general. Exams weigh a lot but are mostly multiple choice. Truly cares about student, good office hours and GREAT response time.
Wonderful professor who cared about his students learning and made accounting fun. Looked forward to this class every Monday & Wednesday night.

Amazing professor, very understanding and can tell he truly cares about his students success. Truly blessed I got him as my Pre-Calc 2 professor :)
